# Azam Khan arrested by ED in Jauhar University case, sent to 14-day judicial custody
Reported By: [Atul Bhatia ](https://www.indiatvnews.com/author/atul-bhatia "Atul Bhatia") Written By: [India TV News Desk ](https://www.indiatvnews.com/author/india-tv-news-desk "India TV News Desk")
Published: Nov 01, 2026, 07:20 PM IST,Updated: Nov 01, 2026, 11:48 PM IST
## Samajwadi Party leader and former Uttar Pradesh minister Azam Khan has been sent to 14 days' judicial custody in an alleged money laundering case linked to Jauhar University. He has been taken to Dasna jail.
Azam Khan has already been taken to Dasna jail. Image Source : PTI
Samajwadi Party leader and former Uttar Pradesh Cabinet minister Azam Khan has been sent to 14 days' judicial custody in an alleged money laundering case.
The Directorate of Enforcement's Lucknow Zonal Office arrested Azam Khan on October 31, 2026, under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002. A special PMLA court in Ghaziabad remanded him to judicial custody. He has already been taken to Dasna jail.
### **ED's investigation into alleged land grab**
[The ED began its investigation](https://www.indiatvnews.com/uttar-pradesh/ed-attaches-azam-khan-s-jauhar-university-worth-rs-1170-crore-in-money-laundering-case-2026-10-28-1058149) after 26 FIRs were registered by Uttar Pradesh Police at Azeem Nagar police station in Rampur in July 2019. The cases alleged that agricultural land belonging to farmers in Singankhera village was forcibly occupied for the university.
According to the allegations, farmers were subjected to assault, unlawful confinement and threats to make them execute sale deeds in favour of the university.
During its investigation, the ED found that funds and materials meant for public works were allegedly diverted to the university. Government works were carried out on its private campus, while donations from contractors who had been awarded government contracts were allegedly routed back to the trust.
Following information provided by the ED, an FIR under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, and the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, was registered on October 13, 2026. The agency also took up 28 other FIRs registered in Rampur involving allegations of robbery, extortion, cheating and forgery.
### **University property attached, value pegged at Rs 1,170 crore**
On October 28, 2026, the ED provisionally attached land and buildings of the university held by the trust, valued at Rs 426.46 crore, under the PMLA. The present value of the attached property is estimated at around Rs 1,170 crore.
The agency had earlier conducted searches at the university and related premises in Rampur in August 2026. Incriminating documents and electronic devices were seized during the searches.
Further investigation is in progress.

# 'Azam the, Azam hain': Will the Khan factor help or haunt Akhilesh in 2027 UP elections?
[Pallavi](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/toireporter/author-pallavi-479265953.cms) / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Nov 02, 2026, 18:57 IST

[Print](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/articleshowprint/135462603.cms "print article")
The SP chief’s public show of support for the veteran leader comes amid questions over the Azam Khan family’s influence on the party’s prospects ahead of the 2027 elections.
NEW DELHI: "Azam the, Azam hain aur Azam rahenge" (Azam was, Azam is and Azam will remain).With that emphatic declaration, [Samajwadi Party](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/topic/samajwadi-party) chief [Akhilesh Yadav](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/topic/akhilesh-yadav) sought to end speculation about his equation with one of the party's tallest Muslim leaders. But the political reality surrounding Mohammad [Azam Khan](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/topic/azam-khan) is far more complicated than the slogan suggests.Nine days after Akhilesh's October 22 visit to Azam at Rampur jail, the veteran leader walked out of prison with his son Abdullah Azam after the Allahabad high court granted them bail in the dual PAN card case. His freedom, however, lasted barely minutes. The Enforcement Directorate arrested him in a separate money-laundering case linked to Mohammad Ali Jauhar University, and a court subsequently remanded him to 14 days' judicial custody.The dramatic turn has put Akhilesh's declaration to the test. Once among the most powerful figures in the SP, Azam remains central to the party's political calculations in Rampur and its relationship with Muslim voters. But his legal battles, the erosion of his family's electoral stronghold and the growing challenge from Asaduddin Owaisi have turned his return into a complicated political proposition.As Uttar Pradesh heads towards the 2027 assembly election, Akhilesh faces a question that goes beyond personal loyalty: can he hold on to Azam's political legacy without becoming hostage to its baggage?
## The brief freedom
Azam and Abdullah had been in custody since November 2025 following their conviction in the dual PAN card case. The Allahabad high court's order suspended their 10-year sentences and granted them bail, paving the way for their release.However, the ED had a separate case waiting. The agency arrested Azam shortly after he walked out of Rampur jail, while Abdullah was allowed to go home.
Azam Khan’s rise in SP was closely tied to his long-standing association with Mulayam Singh Yadav. 
The money-laundering investigation relates to alleged financial irregularities in the construction of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur. The ED has alleged that government funds were diverted for the university's construction. Azam is the founder of the university and heads the trust that runs it. These are allegations being investigated by the agency, not findings of guilt in the present case.Speaking to reporters after his release, Azam alleged that he was being punished for being a Muslim and for establishing a university and schools. "What is there left to say? What can I say? The law has ceased to exist. Is this the punishment for being a Muslim?" he said.The following day, a special PMLA court in Ghaziabad sent him to 14 days' judicial custody. The court proceedings ensured that the brief release did not translate into a return to political activity.
## Akhilesh turns arrest into political battle
Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav responded sharply to the ED action, accusing the BJP government of using cases to repeatedly send an elderly political leader to jail.In a post on X, the SP chief said: "Let today's rulers remember that thrones change when the time changes. The conspiracy being hatched against Mr Azam Khan through these cases is being watched not just by the entire country, but by the whole world."He added that repeatedly implicating an elderly man in cases and sending him to jail was "an utterly cowardly act", warning that injustice could eventually turn into a calamity for those responsible.The response was significant because it came barely nine days after Akhilesh had visited Azam in jail. That meeting had already signalled that the SP chief was unwilling to distance himself from the veteran leader despite the legal controversies surrounding him.The ED arrest has now sharpened the political messaging. For Akhilesh, the issue is no longer simply Azam's return to the party's political fold. It is also about positioning the SP against what it describes as the misuse of investigative agencies to target opposition leaders.The BJP, on the other hand, has defended the ED action, maintaining that the law applies equally to everyone.
## The Muslim vote and the Owaisi challenge
For the Samajwadi Party, the stakes in the Azam Khan question go well beyond the fortunes of one leader. They concern the party's hold over a crucial section of its traditional support base: Muslim voters. Muslims account for roughly 19% of Uttar Pradesh's population, making them one of the state's largest voting blocs. Their concentration in several constituencies gives them considerable electoral influence. In the 2022 assembly election, the community was a decisive factor in around 70 constituencies where Muslims formed at least 30% of the population.The 2022 results also showed how strongly the community rallied behind the SP. The party fielded 64 Muslim candidates, of whom 31 won, taking the total number of Muslim MLAs in the assembly to 36, up from 24 in 2017. The BSP fielded 88 Muslim candidates and the Congress 75, while AIMIM fielded more than 60. Yet neither the BSP nor Congress managed to elect a single Muslim MLA. The results suggested that the SP had emerged as the principal beneficiary of Muslim consolidation, even as smaller parties remained relevant in individual constituencies.
Muslims account for at least 30% of the population in around 70 constituencies.
Azam Khan was central to this political equation. His influence in Rampur and his standing among sections of the Muslim community gave the SP an important local and regional network. His electoral record, along with that of his wife Tazeen Fatima and son Abdullah Azam, made the family one of the most prominent Muslim political establishments in the state. His absence from active politics has therefore left a space that other political players may seek to occupy.It is this space that AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi is attempting to enter. His October 18 rally in Tanda was a reminder that the SP cannot take Muslim support for granted. Owaisi accused Akhilesh of treating Muslims as a vote bank while prioritising the Yadav community, and questioned why the SP leadership had not done more for Azam Khan. His pitch was for independent Muslim political representation, arguing that the community should produce its own MLAs and MPs rather than remain a support base for established political families.Owaisi's intervention is significant because the SP's electoral arithmetic depends not just on retaining Muslim support but also on preventing its fragmentation. The 2022 results showed the limits of smaller parties: although BSP and AIMIM fielded substantial numbers of Muslim candidates, neither managed to convert that presence into Muslim representation in the Assembly. However, even without winning seats, such parties can potentially affect the outcome in closely contested constituencies by splitting votes.Akhilesh's October 22 visit to Azam in Rampur jail was therefore also a political signal. His declaration, "Azam they, Azam hain aur Azam rahenge" (Azam was, is and will remain), aimed to reassure the veteran leader's followers that the SP had not abandoned him. The visit came amid growing questions over whether Owaisi could use sympathy for Azam to make inroads among Muslim voters.The challenge is compounded by the SP's wider social coalition strategy. Akhilesh has sought to move beyond the traditional Muslim-Yadav combination through his PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) framework, bringing backward classes, Dalits and minorities under a broader political umbrella. But the party cannot afford to lose its Muslim support base while attempting to expand its reach among other communities.
Owaisi has attacked Akhilesh Yadav over the treatment of Azam Khan's family.
As the 2027 assembly election approaches, Akhilesh faces a delicate balancing act. He must reassure Azam's supporters that the SP continues to value the veteran leader and his political legacy, while ensuring that the party's Muslim support base does not become an opening for Owaisi or other rivals. The 2022 election demonstrated the electoral value of Muslim consolidation behind the SP. The question now is whether Akhilesh can hold that coalition together without relying too heavily on one leader or one political family.
## From kingmaker to political liability?
To understand Akhilesh Yadav's dilemma, one must first understand the extent of Azam Khan's influence in Rampur. For decades, Khan was not just the Samajwadi Party's most powerful face in the district but the man who dominated its political landscape. He challenged the influence of Rampur's erstwhile Nawab family and gradually built a formidable political network, winning the Rampur Sadar assembly seat 10 times. His influence extended beyond his own electoral victories: his wife, Tazeen Fatima, succeeded him as MLA in a 2019 bypoll, while his son Abdullah Azam twice won the Suar assembly seat. The Azam family's political presence became so entrenched that Rampur's electoral fortunes were often seen through the prism of Khan's influence.That hold was not easily broken. In the 2022 assembly election, Azam Khan won Rampur Sadar for the 10th time despite campaigning from jail. The BJP's Akash Saxena, one of his most prominent political adversaries who had pursued several cases against Azam Khan and his family, lost that contest. But the equation changed after Khan was disqualified following his conviction in a hate speech case. In the December 2022 bypoll, Saxena defeated Azam Khan's close aide Asim Raza by around 34,000 votes, delivering the BJP its first victory in Rampur Sadar and making Saxena the first Hindu candidate to win the constituency. The result marked a significant breach in a political stronghold that Khan and his family had dominated for decades.The erosion of the Azam family's influence became more apparent in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. With Khan, his wife and son facing imprisonment, the SP fielded Maulana Mohibullah Nadvi from Rampur. The choice reportedly upset Khan's loyalists, many of whom stayed away from campaigning, exposing a growing rift between the local Azam camp and the party leadership. It was a reminder that Azam Khan's network could still matter to the SP even in his absence, but also that Akhilesh could no longer assume the family would automatically fall in line with the party's decisions.His treatment by the central agencies gives the party an opportunity to frame the issue as one of political targeting and due process. But the party will have to contend with the electoral consequences of being closely associated with a leader whose legal record has become a recurring political flashpoint.The challenge for Akhilesh is to retain the political value of the Azam network without allowing the controversies surrounding Khan and his family to define the SP's wider campaign. In Rampur, the question is no longer simply whether Azam Khan can return to politics. It is whether the political machinery he built can still deliver for the Samajwadi Party, and on whose terms.
## BJP's counter: 'Mafia raj' and law and order
In 2022, UP CM Yogi Adityanath famously said: "Even Akhilesh doesn’t want Azam Khan to come out of jail because it will pose a threat to his position [chair]. The state government has nothing to do with these cases, whether they are related to Azam Khan or anyone else. It is the court that grants bail.""Under previous governments, mafias were running a parallel administration. When we took action against the land mafia who grabbed poor farmers' land for private universities and personal fiefdoms, the Samajwadi Party developed sympathy for criminals instead of the victims," he had said.The above remarks are at the core of the BJP's attack.The BJP has consistently used the Azam Khan issue to attack the Samajwadi Party's record on law and order. The party's broader political narrative has sought to associate the SP's previous tenure with alleged criminal influence and what it describes as 'mafia raj'.That gives the BJP an obvious line of attack if Akhilesh makes Azam's rehabilitation a central political theme. The ruling party can frame the SP's outreach as evidence that it has not moved away from its past.
UP accused Akhilesh of opposing Azam Khan’s release out of concern that the veteran leader could challenge his position in party.
The SP, meanwhile, has to navigate the distinction between allegations, court findings and the political narrative built around them. It can point to the legal process and the need for due process, but it cannot wish away the electoral impact of the cases and convictions.The BJP's attack also puts the SP's broader coalition strategy under pressure. Akhilesh has sought to expand the party's social base beyond its traditional support groups through the PDA framework. A campaign dominated by the Azam Khan controversy could complicate that effort.Akhilesh's jail visit, his response to the ED arrest and the party's continued engagement with Azam Khan send a message to the SP's traditional supporters: the party has not abandoned a leader who played a major role in building its political presence.But the message also carries risks. The SP has to decide how much political space to give the Azam family, how prominently to project its association with them and how to prevent the issue from becoming a defining feature of its 2027 campaign.

# Azam Khan walks out of jail after 11 months, ED takes him into custody within minutes
## Azam Khan alleges he is being punished for being a Muslim; lawyers to challenge action in SC; his son Abdullah walks free on bail
Published on: Nov 1, 2026, 07:41:10 IST
By [Rohit Kumar Singh](https://www.hindustantimes.com/author/rohit-kumar-singh-101608310462932), LUCKNOW
Prefer HTon Google
Share via
Copy link
The prison gates opened on Saturday evening after nearly 11 months behind bars for veteran Samajwadi Party leader and former Uttar Pradesh cabinet minister Azam Khan, but the freedom proved fleeting.
Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan waves following his release from Rampur jail, in Rampur on Saturday. He was taken into custody by the Enforcement Directorate afterwards. (ANI VIDEO GRAB)
Within minutes of securing his release from Rampur district jail along with his son Abdullah Azam in the dual-PAN-card case, Azam Khan was questioned by an Enforcement Directorate (ED) team from Lucknow and taken into custody in connection with a separate money-laundering investigation involving the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust and Mohammad Ali Jauhar University. Abdullah was allowed to walk free.
As ED officials took him away, Azam Khan briefly spoke to reporters outside the jail, alleging that he was being punished for being a Muslim.
“What’s left there to say... It’s the punishment for being a Muslim. The mistake was, a Muslim built the university, this is the crime; made schools for children, this is the crime,” he said when asked to comment on the development.
The dramatic turn began even before the father and son could emerge from the jail. An ED team entered the prison around 15 minutes before their scheduled release at approximately 7.10 pm. Outside, 24 Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) personnel were deployed. The ED officials questioned Azam and then took him away, while several hundred supporters who had gathered to welcome the two leaders watched the sudden reversal.
A senior ED official in Lucknow confirmed the action, saying, “Yes, we have apprehended Azam Khan. After following the arrest procedures, we will formally arrest him and produce him before the Ghaziabad PMLA court on Sunday morning.”
The agency’s action came just two days after the Allahabad high court, on October 29, granted bail to Azam and Abdullah and suspended their sentences in the dual-PAN-card case. The court declined to stay their convictions, but its order paved the way for their release after the necessary legal formalities were completed.
Azam Khan’s legal team termed the ED action unconstitutional and announced plans to approach the Supreme Court. Senior advocate and Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal, who represents Azam, is expected to take up the matter in the apex court against the agency’s action.
The ED action relates to a separate money-laundering investigation involving the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust and Mohammad Ali Jauhar University. The agency has been probing alleged financial irregularities linked to the trust and the university and had earlier questioned Azam in jail in connection with the case. It had also attached properties associated with the university as part of its investigation.
With the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections due in 2027, Azam’s release after nearly 11 months in jail had considerable political significance. On October 22, just nine days before his release, SP president Akhilesh Yadav had visited Rampur jail to meet him.
For Azam, Saturday’s episode marked the end of his third spell in jail since 2020, but not an immediate return to freedom. He was first sent to jail on February 26, 2020, and remained there until May 20, 2022, when he was released after securing interim bail from the Supreme Court. He was jailed again on October 18, 2023, and released on September 23, 2025. His third stint began on November 17, 2025, and ended with the release order on October 31, 2026. The ED action followed almost immediately.
The release had drawn several hundred SP supporters to the jail in anticipation of welcoming the father and son. Their celebrations, however, were short-lived. While Abdullah left the prison premises, Azam was taken away by the ED team, with the agency confirming that it would complete his formal arrest and produce him before the special PMLA court in Ghaziabad on Sunday.
Reacting to ED taking Azam Khan into custody, SP national spokesperson Abbas Haider said, “The Enforcement Directorate and other central agencies appear to have become instruments of political intimidation rather than independent investigative institutions. Their actions against senior Samajwadi Party leader Mohd. Azam Khan Sahib reflect a disturbing pattern of using state and central machinery to target political opponents.”
“Consider the ED’s own figures: out of 8,851 ECIRs registered under PMLA since its inception, trials have been completed in just 60 cases — a mere 0.68%. This raises serious questions about the pace and effectiveness of investigations when people are arrested and subjected to prolonged custody while trials remain pending,” he said.
The BJP government, unable to keep Azam Khan Sahib behind bars through its existing cases, appears determined to implicate him in fresh cases through central agencies. This is nothing short of political vendetta and a grave assault on constitutional rights. The ED must investigate financial crimes, not become a tool for intimidating the Opposition and settling political scores,” he added.

LUCKNOW: In a dramatic development, the Enforcement Directorate (ED) arrested senior Samajwadi Party leader and former MP [Azam Khan](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/topic/azam-khan) outside Rampur district jail on Saturday, moments after he walked out following nearly 11 months in custody. His son, Abdullah Azam, was released and went home.ED officials questioned Khan outside the jail before taking him away in a vehicle.Sources in the agency said he had been arrested in connection with a 2019 Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR) registered under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). He is likely to be produced before a court in Ghaziabad, sources said.As ED officials questioned him, Khan reportedly had a heated exchange with them. Reacting emotionally to his arrest, he said, “What more can I say now? This is the punishment for being a Muslim. The mistake is that a Muslim built a university. That is our crime.”The ED team had reached Rampur jail before Khan's release. Around 24 CRPF personnel were also deployed outside the prison as the agency prepared to take him into custody. The arrest came amid a large gathering of Khan's supporters, who had assembled outside the jail to welcome him after his release.

#  Azam Khan moves Supreme Court against ED detention outside Rampur Jail 
## The detention of senior Samajwadi party leader Azam Khan has happened with the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections in mind, Advocate Pasha said
Published - November 02, 2026 11:18 am IST - NEW DELHI
[ The Hindu Bureau](https://www.thehindu.com/profile/author/the-hindu-bureau-14355/)
READ LATER
[ SEE ALL ](https://www.thehindu.com/myaccount/?tab=bookmarks) Remove 
Samajwadi Party (SP) leader and former Uttar Pradesh Minister Azam Khan arrives to be produced before a court, in Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh, on November 1, 2026 | Photo Credit: PTI 
Senior Samajwadi Party leader [Azam Khan urges Supreme Court to list a plea seeking relief after Directorate of Enforcement](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/uttar-pradesh/ed-detains-sp-leader-azam-khan-from-outside-rampur-jail-as-soon-as-he-comes-out-on-bail/article71650360.ece) (ED) detains him outside Rampur Jail on October 31, 2026[ immediately after he was released on bail](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/uttar-pradesh/samajwadi-party-leader-azam-khan-released-from-jail-after-23-months/article70083843.ece) in an alleged PAN fraud case.
Making an oral mentioning before Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, advocate Nizam Pasha, for the 78-year-old politician, said this was part of what the Supreme Court had itself, on a previous occasion, said an “evergreening of cases” by the State against Mr. Khan with a political motive in mind.
“It was an illegal arrest in a seven-year-old FIR. The purpose is to to delay his eventual release. The Supreme Court had given him relief the previous time,” Advocate Pasha submitted, seeking a hearing this week.
[ Samajwadi Party’s Azam Khan sent to 14-day judicial custody](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/uttar-pradesh/samajwadi-partys-azam-khan-sent-to-14-day-judicial-custody/article71653438.ece)
He said 87 FIRs were filed against his client. This was the 88th one.
The detention has happened with the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections in mind, Advocate Pasha said.
The CJI said since his release immediately prior to the ED detention was on the basis of a Allahabad High Court order, Mr. Khan ought to approach the High Court rather than move the apex court directly.
“Have faith in the High Court, it has given him relief. We will relegate this matter to the High Court and request it to take it up without delay,” the CJI addressed the counsel
Advocate Pasha urged the court to list the petition, and then take whatever decision in its wisdom.
“We will list it this week,” Chief Justice Kant said.

The Enforcement Directorate on Saturday detained Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Azam Khan from outside the Rampur jail in Uttar Pradesh, just as he came out on bail in an alleged PAN fraud case, officials said.

#  ED detains SP leader Azam Khan from outside Rampur jail as soon as he comes out on bail 
## On October 29, the Allahabad High Court suspended the sentence of Azam Khan and his son Abdullah Azam Khan in the alleged dual PAN card case and granted them bail.
Updated  - October 31, 2026 09:51 pm IST - Lucknow
[Mayank Kumar](https://www.thehindu.com/profile/author/mayank-kumar-15607/)
READ LATER
[ SEE ALL ](https://www.thehindu.com/myaccount/?tab=bookmarks) Remove 
Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Azam Khan waves following his release from Rampur jail, in Rampur on Saturday, October 31, 2026. | Photo Credit: ANI 
The Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Saturday (October 31, 2026) detained [senior Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Azam Khan](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/uttar-pradesh/samajwadi-party-leader-azam-khan-released-from-jail-after-23-months/article70083843.ece) from outside the Rampur jail in Uttar Pradesh immediately after he was released on bail in an alleged PAN fraud case, officials said. Mr. Khan, 78, may soon be arrested under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA).
On October 29, the Allahabad High Court suspended the sentence of Mr. Khan and his son Abdullah Azam Khan in the alleged dual PAN card case and granted them bail.
SP president Akhilesh Yadav criticised the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) for the action against Mr. Khan.
“Today’s rulers should remember that when times change, the throne also changes. The conspiracy of filing cases against respected Azam Khan Sahib is being seen not only by the entire country but by the entire world. It is a very cowardly act to trap an elderly person in such frivolous cases and put him in jail again and again. The current government is fostering a wrong trend, and if the wind changes, it will itself become a victim. Then there will be no running away,” he wrote on X.
Sudhir Panwar, a senior SP leader, said Azam Khan’s arrest smacked of political vendetta.
“He is the only leader languishing in jail on frivolous charges just because he established a university for the disadvantaged sections. His words outside the jail highlighted the State’s discrimination against Muslim leaders in implementing the rule of law,” he added.
> #WATCH | Uttar Pradesh | SP leader Azam Khan released from Rampur jail. After his release, an ED team has reportedly taken him into custody in connection with a case registered with the agency The Allahabad High Court has granted relief to former Cabinet Minister Mohammad Azam Khan and his son, former MLA Abdullah Azam Khan, in the two PAN card case. The Court had previously reserved its order after hearing applications seeking a stay on their conviction, suspension of their sentences, and the grant of interim bail.

# Punishment for being a Muslim: Azam Khan arrested moments after release on bail
##  Azam Khan walked out of Rampur jail on bail on Saturday, only to be arrested by the ED in a money laundering case moments later. The SP leader will be produced before a special court in Ghaziabad on Sunday.
Advertisement
Azam Khan was arrested by ED in a money laundering case on Saturday. (PTI photo/ file)
By:[India Today News Desk](https://www.indiatoday.in/author/india-today-news-desk "India Today News Desk")
Lucknow,Oct 31, 2026 21:39 IST
Last UpdatedOct 31, 2026 21:39 IST 
Published by
India Today Web Desk 
Oct 31, 2026 21:39 IST
Edited by[Anuja Jha](https://www.indiatoday.in/author/anuja-jha)
Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Azam Khan was arrested by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) in a money laundering case on Saturday, moments after he was released from Rampur jail on bail in a separate case involving alleged possession of two PAN cards. Azam Khan alleged that he was being targeted for being a Muslim.
The 78-year-old former Uttar Pradesh minister was taken away by an ED team accompanied by CRPF personnel and Uttar Pradesh Police as he stepped out of the jail. He had been lodged there since November 2025.
advertisement
Read Full Story
The agency will produce Khan before a special Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) court in Ghaziabad on Sunday and seek his remand for custodial interrogation, officials said.
Speaking to reporters outside the jail before being taken away, Khan questioned the legal proceedings against him. "What is there left to say? What can I say? The law has ceased to exist. Is this the punishment for being a Muslim? Our mistake was that a university was built by a Muslim. That is our crime. We built schools for children. Is that our crime?" he said.
Khan had been lodged in Rampur jail since November 2025. His release came after the[ Allahabad High Court on Thursday suspended his sentence](https://www.indiatoday.in/india/law-news/story/azam-khan-abdullah-bail-allahabad-high-court-dual-pan-card-case-ptag-3027937-2026-10-29) and granted him bail in a case involving alleged possession of two PAN cards.
The case also involves his son, former MLA Abdullah Azam Khan. The father-son duo had been convicted by a Rampur court in November last year on charges of forgery, cheating, using forged documents and criminal conspiracy.
The case originated from a 2019 complaint by BJP leader Akash Saxena, who alleged that Abdullah had obtained two PAN cards with different dates of birth. The prosecution claimed that the second PAN card was used to make him eligible to contest the 2017 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.
The High Court granted bail to both men but did not stay their convictions.
## ED'S MONEY LAUNDERING CASE
The ED has registered a money laundering case against Khan and others, based on 58 FIRs filed by Uttar Pradesh Police against him and his alleged associates.
On Wednesday, the agency announced that it had [attached land and buildings belonging to Khan's Mohammad Ali Jauhar University](https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/jauhar-university-assets-attached-ed-azam-khan-money-laundering-case-uttar-pradesh-3027079-2026-10-28) in Rampur under the anti-money laundering law. The attached properties have an estimated market value of Rs 1,170 crore.
The ED has alleged that government funds meant for public works were diverted to construct the private university. It has accused Khan of using his influence as the state's Urban Development Minister and as a minister associated with the Uttar Pradesh Jal Nigam to facilitate the alleged irregularities.
advertisement
The Rampur Development Authority had also ordered the demolition of 38 buildings on the university campus in July. The university subsequently filed an appeal against the order.
The ED conducted raids in the case in August and questioned Khan as part of its investigation.
SP chief Akhilesh Yadav has accused the BJP government of political vendetta against Khan, alleging that false cases were filed against his former cabinet colleague.

Senior Samajwadi Party leader and former Uttar Pradesh Cabinet minister was arrested by the Enforcement Directorate in connection with a case registered in under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) soon after **[he stepped out of the Rampur district jail](https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/lucknow/azam-khan-dual-pan-case-allahabad-high-court-bail-granted-10942620/) **on Saturday evening.
Khan, along with his son Abdullah [Azam Khan](https://indianexpress.com/about/azam-khan/), was granted bail by the Allahabad High Court in a **[double PAN card case](https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/lucknow/sp-leader-azam-khan-son-7-year-jail-term-pan-card-forgery-case-10370785/)** two days ago. Abdullah, also lodged in the Rampur jail, went to his home after being released from jail.
The HC, however, had dismissed their plea for staying their conviction and had fixed the hearing in the revision petition in January. The two have been in jail since their sentencing in November last year.
Story continues below.  [Subscribe to see fewer ads.](https://indianexpress.com/express-plus/subscription-plan/?pageCode=15&ref=ad_pos_3)
The case pertained to Abdullah obtaining two PAN cards with different dates of birth, and his father was named as an accomplice in the alleged forgery.
Also Read | [ED attaches Jauhar University land, buildings in money-laundering case](https://indianexpress.com/article/india/ed-jauhar-university-land-money-laundering-case-10940783/)
The ED had registered the PMLA case over alleged financial irregularities in the construction of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur. Azam Khan is the founder of the university and the chairperson of the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust that runs the institution.
He will be produced in a designated court in Ghaziabad on Sunday since the case is being investigated by the agency’s Delhi branch, it is learnt.
The day the hearing of Khan’s bail was going on on Thursday, a team of ED officials from Delhi reached Rampur and launched a day-long search on the university premises and attached the campus land and buildings with a market value of more than Rs 1,000 crore.
Story continues below this ad
The ED had initiated its probe after the Rampur district administration and police started filing cases against Azam and the Trust on charges of constructing the university on the land belonging to government or owned by locals, when the Samajwadi Party was in power in Uttar Pradesh and he was a minister.
Read | [When Akhilesh Yadav met Azam Khan: Inside their jail huddle on UP poll eve](https://indianexpress.com/article/political-pulse/up-polls-to-owaisi-why-akhilesh-yadav-met-azam-khan-in-rampur-jail-10934512/)
The agency had alleged that government funds were diverted for developing the university and that government departments carried out the construction work on the campus.
On October 13, the Rampur police also lodged another case against Khan and the Trust under charges under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Prevention of Corruption Act in connection with alleged financial irregularities in the construction of the university.
**High-voltage drama outside jail**
While his supporters were waiting for Azam Khan outside the jail, the ED team accompanied by a large contingent of CRPF personnel arrived there around 5.30 pm.
Story continues below this ad
The jail authorities had received the bail documents as formalities were completed earlier in the day, an official said.
As soon as Azam and Abdullah walked out of the jail gate around 6.30 pm amid sloganeering by their supporters, the ED officials approached him and showed some him documents apparently related to an arrest order.
The SP leader was seen shouting at the agency officials who asked him to accompany them. After a heated argument, Azam said addressing the mediapersons standing nearby, “ _Kya kahne ko hai. Kahne ko raha kya hai. Musalman hone ki saza hai. Galati ye hai..university banayi ek Musalman ne. Ye hai gunaah. Bachchon ke school banaye. Ye hai gunaah hamara_ (What is left to say. This is the punishment for being a Muslim. This is the offence. A Muslim set up an university. This is the offence. Established schools for children. This is my offence).”
Azam, who faces 92 FIRs lodged against him since 2019, has been convicted in nine cases, including the one in which he got the bail two days ago. There are 81 cases pending in different courts against him.
Story continues below this ad
Soon after Azam’s arrest by the ED, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav posted a message on X, “Let today’s rulers remember that thrones change when the time changes. The conspiracy being hatched against Mr Azam Khan through these cases is being watched not just by the entire country, but by the whole world. To implicate an elderly man in false cases and repeatedly throw them into jail is an utterly cowardly act. When injustice crosses all limits, it turns into a calamity for the oppressor themselves. Utterly condemnable.”

# Azam Khan Moves Supreme Court Against ED Arrest In Money Laundering Case
2 Nov 2026 11:59 AM2 Nov 2026 11:59 AM
## The Supreme Court declines urgent listing of the plea; SP leader was sent to 14-day judicial custody by a Ghaziabad court.
Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan has approached the Supreme Court challenging his arrest by the Enforcement Directorate in a money laundering case linked to the Jauhar Trust.
[ As PreferredSource ](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=deccanchronicle.com)
Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan on Monday moved the Supreme Court challenging his arrest in a fresh money laundering case by the Enforcement Directorate (ED).A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana took note of submissions of Khan's lawyer Nizam Pasha and said that the plea may be listed during the week.
The bench, however, refused urgent listing of the plea. On Sunday, a special Ghaziabad court sent Khan to judicial custody for 14 days. The SP veteran was produced before the special Ghaziabad court in connection with the money laundering case related to the Jauhar Trust, Khan's lawyer had said.
Earlier, Khan was brought to the court under heavy security as scores of his supporters stood outside the premises to catch a glimpse of their leader, who has been battling a series of legal cases filed against him over the past few years.
The ED arrested Khan on October 31 in the money laundering case shortly after he and his son Abdullah Azam Khan were released from Rampur jail on bail in an alleged dual PAN card case. The agency had conducted raids in the case in August and also questioned Khan. Khan has also been facing various criminal cases.

# Senior SP leader Azam Khan sends to 14-day judicial custody in money laundering case
Khan will be lodged in Dasna District Jail in Ghaziabad instead of Rampur jail, from where he had been released on Saturday.
Senior Samajwadi Party leader and former lawmaker Azam Khan.File Photo.
Updated on: 
01 Nov 2026, 8:50 am
2 min read
  * Copied


LUCKNOW: Senior Samajwadi Party leader and former lawmaker Azam Khan was remanded to 14 days of judicial custody by a special Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) court in Ghaziabad on Sunday.
Khan will be lodged in Dasna District Jail in Ghaziabad instead of Rampur jail, from where he had been released on Saturday.
As per the sources, the Enforcement Directorate (ED) produced Azam Khan before Special Judge Anti-Corruption CBI court, Avanish Kumar Pandey at around 10.30 am amid tight security. A convoy of five ED vehicles brought him to the court premises, accompanied by more than 100 personnel from the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) and the Uttar Pradesh Police.
Khan appeared calm when he arrived at the court in a MUV car. As he rolled down the window, journalists asked whether he wanted to say something. He responded, "Ab kya reh gaya hai bolne ko" (What is left to say now?).
The court gave the order after hearing the matter for about 90 minutes. The ED counsel, Kuldeep Srivastava, argued on behalf of the agency, while ED’s Deputy Director Piyush Thorat and Assistant Director Praveen Kumar remained present inside the court.
The court's order came after the ED arrested Khan on Saturday evening in connection with a money laundering case registered by the agency in 2019. He was taken into custody shortly after being released from Rampur District Jail and was subsequently brought to the ED headquarters in Delhi for questioning.
[ SP leader Azam Khan taken into ED custody soon after walking out of Rampur jail](https://www.newindianexpress.com/states/uttar-pradesh/2026/Oct/31/sp-leader-azam-khan-taken-into-ed-custody-soon-after-walking-out-of-rampur-jail)
Thereafter, Azam complained of a chest and stomachache, following which a team of CRPF and ED took the former minister to RML hospital in Delhi and got him checked up. After clearance from a specialist team of doctors at the RML, he was brought to ED HQ and questioned again.
According to officials, Khan was questioned at length in connection with the alleged misuse of government funds in the construction of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur. During the interrogation, the agency reportedly put more than 50 questions to him as part of its investigation into the alleged financial irregularities.
Khan and his son, Abdullah Azam, had walked out of Rampur jail at around 7.15 pm on Saturday after spending nearly 11 months in custody. His release had become possible after the Allahabad High Court, on October 29, suspended his 10-year sentence in the two PAN card case.
However, his release proved short-lived, as the ED arrested him in the money laundering case before he could return to normal life outside prison.
The developments triggered sharp political reactions. Samajwadi Party national general secretary Shivpal Singh Yadav criticised the government, alleging that the ED acted at its behest to arrest Khan immediately after his release from jail. He called upon people to speak out against what he described as oppressive governments.
BJP leaders, on the other hand, defended the ED's action, maintaining that the law was equal for everyone.
Uttar Pradesh Energy Minister AK Sharma said that the law applies equally to everyone, irrespective of their position or identity. He remarked that people sometimes disregard the law when they become consumed by the arrogance of power, but eventually everyone has to face its consequences.

Synopsis
Mohammad Azam Khan has approached the Supreme Court to challenge his arrest by the Enforcement Directorate. Agencies
SP leader Azam Khan challenges ED arrest in Supreme Court, plea to be heard later this week
New Delhi: Senior SP leader [Mohammad Azam Khan](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/topic/mohammad-azam-khan) has approached the SC challenging his arrest by the ED, hours after walking out of Rampur jail following his release on bail in a separate case.The matter was mentioned before a bench headed by CJI Surya Kant on Monday by advocate Nizam Pasha. However, the HC declined to stay his conviction. ED arrested Khan in connection with a [money laundering investigation](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/topic/money-laundering-investigation) into alleged financial irregularities in the construction of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur.

ED arrests SP leader Azam Khan in Jauhar University-linked money laundering
##  ED arrests SP leader Azam Khan in Jauhar University-linked money laundering 
  * by [ indiatribune](https://www.indiatribune.com/public/index.php/ed-arrests-sp-leader-azam-khan-in-jauhar-university-linked-money-laundering)
  * November 01, 2026 
_2 minutes_ 

Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan walks out of Rampur District Jail following his release after securing bail in the dual PAN card case involving his son Abdullah Azam, in Rampur, Uttar Pradesh, on Saturday, October 31, 2026. (Photo: IANS/Video Grab)
**Ghaziabad, Oct 31 (IANS)** The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has arrested Samajwadi Party leader and former minister Mohammad Azam Khan in a money laundering case, an official said on Saturday. 
Azam Khan will soon be produced before the Special Court (PMLA), Ghaziabad, for custody proceedings, the official said in a statement.
The Samajwadi Party leader’s arrest by the ED comes close to the provisional attachment of land and buildings belonging to Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Uttar Pradesh's Rampur district, valued at Rs 426.46 crore, in connection with the money laundering probe involving the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust, Azam Khan, and others.
The fresh trouble for the Azam Khan came in the backdrop of a short-lived relief offered to him and his son Abdullah Khan by the Allahabad High Court by suspending their sentence in the dual PAN card case and also granted them bail on Thursday. 
In the money laundering case, the ED attached assets of the University that have a current estimated market value of around Rs 1,170 crore.
The university campus, located at Jauhar Nagar in Rampur's Singhankhera village, is owned by the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust, which was founded and is controlled by Azam Khan, who also serves as the institution's honorary Chancellor, said the ED.
The investigation stems from 26 FIRs registered at Azeem Nagar police station in Rampur, alleging that agricultural land belonging to farmers was forcibly acquired for the university.
The ED said enquiries by the district administration also found that nearly 34 acres of enemy property at Singhankhera village had allegedly been occupied for the university despite the cancellation of the land lease. The land has since been recovered by the Custodian of Enemy Property through the district administration.
The agency claimed its investigation revealed that funds intended for public works were diverted to the university, government-funded projects were executed on the private campus, and money from contractors awarded government contracts was routed back to the trust as donations.
The ED has also taken up the investigation of 28 additional FIRs registered against Azam Khan and others in Rampur. These cases include allegations that several houses were demolished in 2016 and that material and equipment linked to public projects were diverted for use at the university campus. The allegations are part of charge sheets filed by the police.
According to the agency, contractors involved in government projects admitted to supplying construction material and funds for the university.
The ED further alleged that proceeds generated through illegal activities were utilised for the acquisition, construction and development of the university and associated assets.
A valuation conducted by the District Valuation Officer estimated the total cost of the university campus, including 59 buildings and land acquired through 114 sale deeds, at Rs 499.09 crore. However, the trust reportedly accounted for only Rs 78.32 crore as capital expenditure in its income tax filings.
After examining the records, the ED concluded that only Rs 72.63 crore of the campus cost could be explained through legitimate sources, leaving Rs 426.46 crore as alleged proceeds of crime.
The agency further alleged that works worth Rs 6.60 crore were executed on the university campus using MLA and MLC local area development funds, while government sanctions amounting to Rs 23.41 crore were granted for infrastructure projects on the private campus. The ED claimed that subsequent modifications to government orders resulted in public assets being transferred to the university.
Based on these findings, the ED has attached the university's land and buildings to the extent of the alleged proceeds of crime of Rs 426.46 crore.
Searches conducted at the university and related premises on August 19, 2026, resulted in the seizure of electronic devices and documents, the agency said.

# Azam Khan Moves SC Against ED Arrest In Fresh Money Laundering Case
## Khan was arrested by ED on Saturday, shortly after he and his son were released from Rampur jail in an alleged dual PAN cards case.
Samajwadi Party (SP) national general secretary Azam Khan and his son Mohd Abdullah Azam Khan (IANS)
By  [Sumit Saxena](https://www.etvbharat.com/author/Sumit-Saxena)
Published : November 2, 2026 at 12:00 PM IST 
1 Min Read
**New Delhi:** Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan on Monday moved the Supreme Court against his arrest in a fresh money laundering case by the Enforcement Directorate (ED).
A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana took note of submissions by advocate Nizam Pasha, representing Khan. The bench indicated that the plea may be listed during the week. However, the bench declined to urgently list the plea.
Khan was arrested by the ED on Saturday, shortly after he and his son Abdullah Azam Khan were released from Rampur jail on bail in an alleged dual PAN cards case. He was remanded to 14 days' judicial custody by a special court in Ghaziabad.
The ED registered the money laundering case based on 58 FIRs filed by the Uttar Pradesh Police against Khan and his alleged associates. The central agency accused him of diverting government funds meant for public works to construct the private Jauhar University in Rampur.
The central agency, on October 28, attached land and buildings belonging to the university, with an estimated market value of Rs 1,170 crore. ED sought his custody for questioning over alleged financial transactions and benami property transfers.

# ED arrests SP leader Azam Khan minutes after release from Rampur jail
## Azam Khan's legal team termed the ED action unconstitutional. Senior advocate Kapil Sibal, who represents Khan, is expected to take up the matter in SC.
Updated on: Nov 1, 2026, 07:45:15 IST
By [Rohit Kumar Singh](https://www.hindustantimes.com/author/rohit-kumar-singh-101608310462932)
Prefer HTon Google
Share via
Copy link
An [Enforcement Directorate](https://www.hindustantimes.com/topic/enforcement-directorate) (ED) team from Lucknow on Saturday took veteran Samajwadi Party leader [Azam Khan](https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/lucknow-news/false-cases-can-t-keep-him-imprisoned-forever-akhilesh-backs-azam-khan-after-meeting-in-rampur-jail-101792676236464.html) into custody from outside [Rampur](https://www.hindustantimes.com/topic/rampur) district jail in connection with a money-laundering probe, moments after he was released alongside his son Abdullah Azam after spending 11 months behind bars after being convicted in the dual PAN card case.
Officials said Azam Khan was questioned about financial irregularities linked to the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust and Mohammad Ali Jauhar University. (ANI Video Grab)
Officials said Khan was questioned about financial irregularities linked to the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust and Mohammad Ali Jauhar University, and had also questioned Azam while he was still in jail. The central agency has also attached properties associated with the university as part of its investigation.
The ED team entered jail premises around 15 minutes before Khan and Abdullah’s scheduled release, they said. 24 CRPF personnel were deployed outside the premises, where hundreds of SP supporters gathered in anticipation of the release. Abdullah was allowed to walk free.
“After following the arrest procedures, we will formally arrest him and produce him (Khan) before the Ghaziabad PMLA court on Sunday morning,” said a senior official.
The move came two days after the Allahabad high court quashed the father and son’s sentences in the dual PAN card case and granted bail, despite refusing to stay their sentences.
Speaking to reporters outside the jail, Khan said he was being punished for being a Muslim. “The mistake was that a Muslim built the university, this is the crime; made schools for children, this is the crime,” he said.
Khan’s legal team termed the ED action unconstitutional. Senior advocate and Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal, who represents Khan, is expected to take up the matter in the Supreme Court.
The action against Khan also came against the backdrop of intensifying preparations for the state assembly elections in 2027. Earlier, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav met him at the jail on October 22. SP national spokesperson Abbas Haider alleged that the “BJP government,unable to keep Azam Khan Sahib behind bars through its existing cases, appears determined to implicate him in fresh cases through central agencies.”
“Consider the ED’s own figures— out of 8,851 ECIRs registered under PMLA since its inception, trials have been completed in just 60 cases — a mere 0.68%. This raises serious questions about the pace and effectiveness of probes when people are arrested and subjected to prolonged custody while trials remain pending,” he added .

# 'Ab kya reh gaya hai bolne ko': Azam Khan sent to 14-day judicial custody; to be lodged in Ghaziabad jail
[Pathikrit Chakraborty](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/toireporter/author-Pathikrit-Chakraborty-479244396.cms) / TNN / Updated: Nov 01, 2026, 14:11 IST

Senior Samajwadi Party leader and former MP Azam Khan
LUCKNOW: Senior [Samajwadi Party](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/topic/samajwadi-party) leader and former MP [Azam Khan](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/topic/azam-khan) was remanded to 14 days of judicial custody by a special Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) court in Ghaziabad on Sunday. He will be lodged in Dasna District Jail in Ghaziabad instead of Rampur jail, from where he had been released barely a day earlier.The [Enforcement Directorate](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/topic/enforcement-directorate) (ED) produced Azam Khan before Special Judge Avanish Kumar Pandey of the Anti-Corruption CBI court at around 10.30 am amid tight security. A convoy of five ED vehicles brought him to the court premises, accompanied by more than 100 personnel from the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) and the Uttar Pradesh Police.
[ Watch Rampur Court Sentences Azam Khan To 2 Years In 2019 Speech Case, SP Veteran Faces Fresh Legal Blow](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/videos/news/rampur-court-sentences-azam-khan-to-2-years-in-2019-speech-case-sp-veteran-faces-fresh-legal-blow/videoshow/131135128.cms)
Khan appeared calm when he arrived at the court in an MUV. As he rolled down the window, journalists asked whether he wanted to say something. He responded, "Ab kya reh gaya hai bolne ko" (What is left to say now?).The court passed the order after hearing the matter for about 90 minutes. ED counsel Kuldeep Srivastava argued on behalf of the agency, while ED Deputy Director Piyush Thorat and Assistant Director Praveen Kumar were also present in the courtroom. ED sources said 26 cases were registered against Azam Khan in 2019, following which the agency lodged ECIR/07/LKZO/2019 on August 1, 2019 under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). During the investigation, the ED alleged that Khan had illegally occupied farmers' land to establish the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust/Mohammad Ali Jauhar University Trust in Rampur. The agency further claimed that illegal collections were made from contractors and others during the construction of the university, generating proceeds of crime worth Rs 426 crore.In its order, the court observed that the gravity of the allegations, the magnitude of the alleged proceeds of crime, and the need for a fair probe into the money trail and related evidence warranted Khan's judicial custody, ED counsel Kuldeep Srivastava told TOI. Khan has been remanded to judicial custody for 14 days and will be produced before the court again on November 13, 2026.The court also directed the Superintendent of District Jail, Ghaziabad, to ensure that Khan receives all necessary medical care in accordance with prison rules and that the medicines prescribed to him are made available during his incarceration.The court's order came after the ED arrested the senior SP leader on Saturday evening in connection with a money laundering case registered by the agency in 2019. He was taken into custody shortly after being released from Rampur District Jail and was subsequently brought to the ED headquarters in Delhi for questioning.Thereafter, Azam complained of chest and stomach pain, following which a team of CRPF and ED personnel took the former minister to RML Hospital in Delhi for a medical examination. After receiving clearance from a specialist team of doctors at RML Hospital, he was brought back to the ED headquarters and questioned again.According to officials, Khan was questioned at length in connection with the alleged misuse of government funds in the construction of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur. During the interrogation, the agency reportedly put more than 50 questions to him as part of its investigation into the alleged financial irregularities.Khan and his son, Abdullah Azam, had walked out of Rampur jail at around 7.15 pm on Saturday after spending nearly 11 months in custody. His release had become possible after the Allahabad High Court, on October 29, suspended his 10-year sentence in the two PAN card cases.However, his release proved short-lived, as the ED arrested him in the money laundering case before he could return to normal life outside prison.The developments triggered sharp political reactions. Uttar Pradesh Energy Minister AK Sharma said the law applied equally to everyone, irrespective of their position or identity. He remarked that people sometimes disregard the law when consumed by the arrogance of power, but eventually everyone has to face its consequences.Meanwhile, Samajwadi Party national general secretary Shivpal Singh Yadav criticised the government, alleging that the ED had acted at its behest to arrest Khan immediately after his release from jail. He called upon people to speak out against what he described as oppressive governments.BJP leaders, on the other hand, defended the ED's action, maintaining that the law was equal for everyone. Bihar BJP president Sanjay Saraogi said the case should not be linked to any particular community and accused Khan of attempting to portray himself as a victim.

# ED attaches SP leader Azam Khan's university in money laundering probe
Source: PTI - Edited By: [Senjo M R](https://www.rediff.com/author/Senjo%20M%20R) October 29, 2026 01:03 IST 5 Minutes Read
Share this Article
**Discover how the Enforcement Directorate has provisionally attached properties worth Rs 1,170 crore belonging to Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan's Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Uttar Pradesh, citing alleged money laundering and diversion of public funds.**
IMAGE: A drone view of the Mohammad Ali Jauhar University.Photograph: ANI Screen Grab
### Key Points
  * The Enforcement Directorate on Wednesday attached the land and building of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University, promoted by Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan, under the anti-money laundering law.
  * The federal probe agency alleges that government funds meant for public works were diverted for the construction of the private varsity, which has a current market value of approximately Rs 1,170 crore.
  * Khan, currently jailed, is accused of using his influence as a Cabinet minister for these alleged irregularities, with estimated proceeds of crime at Rs 426.46 crore.
  * The ED's investigation stems from 54 FIRs filed by Uttar Pradesh Police, including allegations of forcible land acquisition from farmers and illegal occupation of enemy property.
  * Further allegations include the demolition of houses of Rampur residents in 2016 and the diversion of municipal corporation machinery and state government funds for university infrastructure.


The Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Wednesday said it has attached the land and building of Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan-promoted Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Uttar Pradesh under the anti-money laundering law.
The federal probe agency alleged that government funds meant for public works were diverted for the construction of the private varsity, which has a current market value of approximately Rs 1,170 crore, located in Rampur district.
It accused the jailed 78-year-old SP leader of using his influence as the Cabinet minister of Urban Development and the Uttar Pradesh Jal Nigam for these alleged irregularities.
## ED's Provisional Attachment And Valuation
A provisional order has been issued under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) to attach the property comprising 59 buildings.
The land and the buildings were registered and constructed at a cost of Rs 499 crore but they currently command a current market value of Rs 1,170 crore, the ED said in a statement.
The Rampur Development Authority (RDA) ordered the demolition of 38 buildings in the university campus in July, following which the varsity filed an appeal.
SP chief Akhilesh Yadav recently met Khan in jail and accused the BJP government of pursuing political vendetta against his former cabinet colleague and alleged that false cases had been lodged against him.
The agency carried out raids in this case in August and also questioned Khan, who is lodged in Rampur jail facing multiple criminal charges.
The ED said the estimated proceeds of the crime in this case are Rs 426.46 crore.
## Allegations Against Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust
"The University campus at Jauhar Nagar, Village Singhankhera, Rampur, is held by the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust, which was founded and is controlled by Mohammad Azam Khan, who is also the honorary Chancellor of the University," it said.
The Lucknow-headquartered trust runs the Muhammad Ali Jauhar University, founded in 2006, and a public school in the Rampur district.
The ED said it has taken cognisance of 54 FIRs filed by Uttar Pradesh Police to move forward with its money laundering investigation against Khan and his trust.
It added that funds meant for public works were "diverted" to the university and government works were executed on its private campus and funds from contractors (who had been allotted government contracts) were routed back to the trust as donations.
## Specific Irregularities And Fund Diversions
The first set of police FIRs filed at the Azeem Nagar police station of Rampur allege that agricultural land of farmers was "forcibly" taken over for the university.
An inquiry report prepared by the Rampur district administration found that 45 plots of enemy property measuring about 34 acres in Singhankhera village were "illegally" occupied by Khan for the university, even after the lease of this land to the trust had been cancelled by the custodian.
The possession of this land has been taken back by the custodian of enemy property, under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), through the Rampur administration, according to the ED.
The second set of police FIRs and charge sheets filed before courts allege that during 2016, the houses of several families in Rampur city, many of whom were tenants of Waqf property, were demolished with bulldozers by a mob allegedly led by the then circle officer and others on the instructions of Khan, the ED said.
The occupants were assaulted, threatened with false criminal cases, and robbed of their cash, jewellery and cattle. The debris from the demolished houses were transported to the university and cleaning machinery purchased for the Rampur municipal corporation were also "diverted" to the university.
It was found that works worth Rs 6.60 crore were executed at the university using MLA/MLC local area development funds. These works were executed by the Uttar Pradesh Jal Nigam, of which Khan was then the chairman, the ED claimed.
It added that the trust received donations worth Rs 6.24 crore from two Meerut-based educational entities through political influence.
The ED alleged that a public 'pandal' was created in the university using Rs 12 crore state government funds but it was converted into a private property of the educational institution during 2015-16 when Khan was a cabinet minister of the departments that created the said infrastructure.
## Contractor Statements And Further Allegations
The agency recorded the statement of the managing director of a company which received PWD contracts worth Rs 186 crore.
He "admitted" that 30-40 per cent of the contract value was used to buy construction material for the university. The partners of another firm admitted that they operated "under the influence of" Khan to donate Rs 40 lakh to the said trust, it said.

# ED arrests Azam Khan in PMLA case as he walks out of jail on bail
Source: PTI - Edited By: [Senjo M R](https://www.rediff.com/author/Senjo%20M%20R) Updated: October 31, 2026 23:41 IST 4 Minutes Read
Listen to this article [ Watch on Rediff TV](https://tv.rediff.com/news/ed-arrests-azam-khan-in-pmla-case-as-he-walks-out-of-jail-on-bail/411285) Share this Article
**Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan faces a money laundering investigation by the Enforcement Directorate, leading to his arrest on Saturday shortly after securing bail in another case, highlighting ongoing legal challenges for the former Uttar Pradesh minister.**
IMAGE: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan waves following his release from Rampur jail, in Rampur, Uttar Pradesh, October 31, 2026. Photograph: ANI Video Grab
### Key Points
  * Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan was arrested by the Enforcement Directorate on Saturday in a money laundering case.
  * The arrest happened shortly after Khan and his son, Abdullah Azam Khan, were released from Rampur jail on bail in an alleged dual PAN cards case.
  * The ED's money laundering case stems from 58 FIRs registered by the Uttar Pradesh Police against Khan and his associates.
  * The agency recently attached land and buildings of Khan's Mohammad Ali Jauhar University, valued at Rs 1,170 crore, alleging diversion of government funds.
  * Khan claimed his arrest was "punishment for being a Muslim," a sentiment echoed by SP chief Akhilesh Yadav.


The Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Saturday arrested Samajwadi Party (SP) leader and former Uttar Pradesh minister Azam Khan in a money laundering case, shortly after he and his son Abdullah Azam Khan were released from Rampur jail on bail in an alleged dual PAN cards case, officials said.
## Legal Proceedings And Allegations
The 78-year-old leader will be produced before a special Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) court in Ghaziabad on Sunday, where the agency will seek his remand for custodial interrogation, they said.
Khan was arrested by officials of the ED's Lucknow zone amid a heavy deployment of central paramilitary forces and Uttar Pradesh Police personnel.
## Khan's Response And Political Reactions
Speaking to reporters outside Rampur district jail, where he had been lodged since November 2025, Khan said, "Kehne ko kya hai (there is nothing to say)… this is a punishment for being a Muslim… the mistake is that a Muslim made a university and school for students…"
He also raised his hand to greet supporters, who were heard raising slogans in his favour.
SP chief Akhilesh Yadav, speaking to reporters outside Lucknow airport, said, "Do not expect that you will get justice from the BJP."
Asked about Khan's remark that he was being punished for being a Muslim, Yadav said whatever the former minister had said was true, adding that people could not expect justice from the BJP.
## ED's Investigation Into University Funds
Khan and his son secured relief from the Allahabad High Court on Thursday after it suspended their sentences in the dual PAN cards case.
The ED has registered a money laundering case against Khan and others, taking cognisance of 58 FIRs registered by the Uttar Pradesh Police against him and his alleged associates.
On Wednesday, the agency said it had attached the land and buildings of Khan's Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur under the anti-money laundering law. The assets have a current market value of Rs 1,170 crore, it said.
The agency alleged that government funds meant for public works were diverted to construct the private university. It accused Khan of using his influence as the state's cabinet minister for urban development and the Uttar Pradesh Jal Nigam to facilitate the alleged irregularities.
The Rampur Development Authority had ordered the demolition of 38 buildings on the university campus in July, following which the university filed an appeal.
Yadav had recently met Khan in jail and accused the BJP government of pursuing a political vendetta against his former cabinet colleague, alleging that false cases had been lodged against him.
The ED conducted raids in the case in August and also questioned Khan.

#  SP leader Azam Khan moves Supreme Court against ED arrest right after jail release 
##  A Supreme Court bench headed by CJI Surya Kant agreed to hear Azam Khan's petition challenging his ED arrest and judicial remand. 
Written by: [Ananthakrishnan G](https://indianexpress.com/profile/author/ananthakrishnan-g/)
2 min read _New Delhi_ Updated: Nov 3, 2026 05:19 AM IST
Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan amid heavy security following his release from Rampur jail, in Rampur on Saturday. (ANI videograb)

[Samajwadi Party (SP)](https://indianexpress.com/about/samajwadi-party/) leader Azam Khan Monday moved the [Supreme Court](https://indianexpress.com/about/supreme-court/) challenging his arrest and judicial remand by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) on money laundering charges. He was **[arrested Saturday shortly after his release on bail](https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/lucknow/ed-arrests-azam-khan-pmla-case-rampur-jail-10945274/)** in a separate case involving dual PAN cards.
Appearing for Khan, advocate Nizam Pasha mentioned the matter before a bench led by Chief Justice of India (CJI) [Surya Kant](https://indianexpress.com/about/surya-kant/) and requested an urgent hearing. The CJI-led bench said it would list the petition for hearing this week.
The Allahabad High Court**[granted bail to Azam Khan and his son Abdullah Azam Khan](https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/lucknow/azam-khan-dual-pan-case-allahabad-high-court-bail-granted-10942620/)** on October 29 in the dual PAN card case, while dismissing their plea to stay their conviction.
Story continues below.  [Subscribe to see fewer ads.](https://indianexpress.com/express-plus/subscription-plan/?pageCode=15&ref=ad_pos_3)
After stepping out of Rampur jail on the evening of October 31, the agency immediately took Khan into custody over alleged financial irregularities in the construction of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur. His son Abdullah was released and returned home.
## Dual PAN case
On November 27, 2025, a Rampur trial court **[sentenced both to a maximum of seven years of rigorous imprisonment](https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/lucknow/sp-leader-azam-khan-son-7-year-jail-term-pan-card-forgery-case-10370785/)** under charges of criminal conspiracy, cheating, and forgery. An appellate court then enhanced [Azam Khan](https://indianexpress.com/about/azam-khan/)’s sentence to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment.
According to the prosecution, Abdullah had an initial PAN card with a birth date of January 1, 1993, matching his high school certificate, which he used to operate a bank account at the State Bank of India and file income tax returns.
However, when filing nomination papers for the Swar constituency as an SP candidate on January 24, 2017, in Rampur, he allegedly presented a second PAN card showing a birth date of September 30, 1990. The FIR alleged a planned conspiracy between father and son to forge documents to overcome age-eligibility constraints for the election.
Story continues below. [Subscribe to see fewer ads.](https://indianexpress.com/express-plus/subscription-plan/?pageCode=15&ref=ad_pos_2)
In granting bail, the High Court noted that Khan had completed four years, one month, and nine days in prison, including remission, as per a custody certificate dated May 29. Abdullah had undergone three years, six months, and 13 days, as per his custody certificate dated May 30.

# SC to hear Azam Khan's plea against ED arrest in money laundering case this week
##  The Supreme Court said Azam Khan's challenge to his latest ED arrest may be heard this week. The case deepens scrutiny of alleged financial irregularities involving the Jauhar Trust and university.
Advertisement
Azam Khan was arrested by ED in a money laundering case on Saturday. (PTI photo/ file)
By:[India Today News Desk](https://www.indiatoday.in/author/india-today-news-desk "India Today News Desk")
Newdelhi,Nov 2, 2026 12:56 IST
Last UpdatedNov 2, 2026 12:56 IST 
Published by
India Today Web Desk 
Nov 2, 2026 11:54 IST
The Supreme Court on Monday said Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan's plea [challenging his arrest by the Enforcement Directorate](https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/azam-khan-arrest-ed-custody-after-bail-pan-card-money-laundering-case-3029544-2026-10-31) in a fresh money laundering case may be listed for hearing during the week, news agency Press Trust of India reported.
A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana took note of submissions by Khan's lawyer, Nizam Pasha, but refused to list the plea urgently. The Chief Justice, however, said it was likely to be heard during the week.
advertisement
Read Full Story
A special court in Ghaziabad on Sunday sent the 78-year-old SP leader to judicial custody for 14 days in connection with the money laundering case related to the Jauhar Trust.
Khan was produced before the court under heavy security, his lawyer said, according to PTI. Scores of his supporters gathered outside the court premises to catch a glimpse of the leader, who has faced several legal cases over the past few years.
The ED arrested Khan on October 31, shortly after he and his son Abdullah Azam Khan were released on bail from Rampur jail in an alleged dual PAN card case.
The agency registered the money laundering case against Khan and others after taking note of 58 FIRs filed by the Uttar Pradesh Police against him and his alleged associates.
On October 28, the ED said it had attached land and buildings belonging to Khan's Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur under the anti-money laundering law. The assets have a current market value of Rs 1,170 crore.
The agency alleged that government funds meant for public works were diverted to build the private university. It accused Khan of using his influence as Uttar Pradesh's urban development minister and over the Uttar Pradesh Jal Nigam to facilitate the alleged irregularities.
The Rampur Development Authority ordered the demolition of 38 buildings on the university campus in July, following which the university filed an appeal. The ED also conducted searches in the case in August and questioned Khan.
Khan, who is facing several criminal cases, has challenged his latest arrest as he remains in judicial custody in the money laundering case linked to the Jauhar Trust.
