# Azam Khan sent to jail in ED case amid Islamophobia, political vendetta allegations
Published: 22 hours ago 
Azam Khan, who alleged he was being targeted for being a Muslim, was sent to judicial custody a day after the ED arrested him moments after his release on bail. 
[ Maktoob  ](https://maktoobmedia.com/public/index.php/author-posts/1/Maktoob)
A special Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) court in Ghaziabad on Sunday, November 1, remanded veteran Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Azam Khan to 14 days’ judicial custody, a day after the Enforcement Directorate (ED) arrested him moments after his release from Rampur jail.
The 78-year-old former Uttar Pradesh minister alleged that he was being targeted for being a Muslim and for establishing a university, while SP chief Akhilesh Yadav accused the BJP government of pursuing a political vendetta through repeated imprisonment and false cases.
Khan had stepped out of Rampur jail on Saturday after the Allahabad High Court suspended his sentence and granted him bail in a case involving the alleged possession of two PAN cards. An ED team accompanied by CRPF personnel and Uttar Pradesh Police took him away outside the jail, where he had been lodged since November 2025.
Speaking to reporters before being taken away, Khan questioned the legal proceedings against him.
“What is there left to say? What can I say? The law has ceased to exist. Is this the punishment for being a Muslim? Our mistake was that a university was built by a Muslim. That is our crime. We built schools for children. Is that our crime?” he said.
Condemning the action, Yadav accused the government of using cases to repeatedly send his former cabinet colleague to jail.
“Today’s rulers should remember that when times change, the throne also changes. The conspiracy of filing cases against respected Azam Khan Sahib is being seen not only by the entire country but by the entire world. It is a very cowardly act to trap an elderly person in such frivolous cases and put him in jail again and again. The current government is fostering a wrong trend, and if the wind changes, it will itself become a victim. Then there will be no running away.”
In a statement, the ED confirmed Khan’s arrest on October 31 and his subsequent remand.
“Directorate of Enforcement, Lucknow Zonal Office, has arrested Mohammad Azam Khan, founder of Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust and Chancellor of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University, Rampur, on 31.10.2026 under the provisions of the PMLA, 2002, in the money laundering case. He has been sent to judicial custody for 14 days by the Hon’ble Special PMLA Court, Ghaziabad,” the official statement issued by the ED states.
The agency said its investigation began with 26 FIRs registered against Khan and others at Rampur’s Azeem Nagar police station in July 2019 under Sections 323, 342, 384, 447, 504 and 506 of the then Indian Penal Code.
The FIRs alleged that agricultural land belonging to farmers in Singankhera village was forcibly occupied for Mohammad Ali Jauhar University. Farmers were allegedly assaulted, unlawfully confined and threatened into signing sale deeds in the university’s favour.
“During the investigation, the ED found that the funds and material meant for public works were diverted to the university, government works were executed on its private campus, and funds from contractors who had been allotted government contracts were routed back to the Trust as donations. On the ED’s information, an FIR under the provisions of the BNS (Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita), 2023 and the PC (Prevention of Corruption) Act, 1988 was registered on 13.10.2026, and 28 other FIRs registered at Rampur for robbery, extortion, cheating and forgery were also taken up for investigation,” the statement added.
The agency also detailed the attachment of university properties held by the trust.
“In this case, ED has also provisionally attached the land and buildings of the University, held by the Trust, to the extent of ₹426.46 crore under the provisions of PMLA on 28.10.2026. The present value of the attached property is around ₹1,170 crore,” it said.
The ED searched the university and related premises in Rampur in August 2026. The agency said it seized incriminating documents and electronic devices during the searches, and that its investigation remains underway.
The university also faces a July order by the Rampur Development Authority directing the demolition of 38 buildings on its campus. It subsequently appealed against the order.
Khan’s release on bail on Saturday followed the Allahabad High Court’s Thursday order suspending his sentence in the PAN card case. His son, former MLA Abdullah Azam Khan, was also granted bail, although the court did not stay either conviction.
The father and son were convicted by a Rampur court in November last year on charges of forgery, cheating, using forged documents and criminal conspiracy. The case originated from a 2019 complaint by BJP leader Akash Saxena, who alleged that Abdullah had obtained two PAN cards with different dates of birth. The prosecution claimed the second card was used to make him eligible to contest the 2017 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.

# Azam Khan Moves Supreme Court Against ED Arrest Post Release In Dual PAN Card Case
Azam Khan was arrested on 31 October, 2026 by the ED shortly after he and his son Abdullah Azam Khan were released on bail from Rampur jail in a dual PAN card case
By - [Aishwarya Iyer ](https://lawbeat.in/aishwarya-iyer)| 
2 Nov 2026 1:51 PM
Azam Khan has moved Supreme Court against his ED detention outside Rampur Jail, soon after release in another case. 
Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan has approached the Supreme Court challenging his arrest by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) allegedly made just 40 minutes after his release in the Dual PAN Card case on October 29, 2026.
Advocate Nizam Pasha mentioned the plea before Chief Justice of India Surya Kant today, seeking an urgent hearing. Khan has challenged the November 1 order passed by the Special Court remanding him to judicial custody in the ED case. The ED arrest relates to a fresh money laundering case linked to the Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust.
On October 30th, the Allahabad High Court had [granted bail](https://lawbeat.in/news-updates/azam-khan-has-92-criminal-cases-abdullah-46-allahabad-hc-refuses-to-suspend-their-convictions-in-dual-pan-card-case-1647497) to Khan and his son Abdullah Azam Khan in a case involving allegations of forging documents to conceal Abdullah's age and secure his nomination for the 2017 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, while refusing to stay their convictions in the case.
A single-judge bench of Justice Samit Gopal observed that there was no justifiable reason to suspend their convictions, particularly in view of the number of criminal cases pending against them and their previous convictions. 
Court also referred to the wider public interest involved in keeping persons with criminal antecedents away from electoral politics. "Substantial efforts have to be undertaken to cleanse the polluted stream of politics by prohibiting people with criminal antecedents so that they do not even conceive of the idea of entering into politics. They should be kept at bay," court observed. 
Court recorded that Azam Khan was involved in 92 criminal cases and had previously been convicted in eight matters. Of these, two convictions were by courts of sessions and six by magistrate courts. His appeals against two magistrate court convictions had also been dismissed. As many as 81 cases were pending against him before different courts. 
Similarly, Abdullah Azam Khan was involved in 46 criminal cases. He had been convicted in four matters by magistrate courts, with his appeals against two of those convictions dismissed. Another 44 cases were pending against him. 
"Thus looking to the criminal antecedents of the accused/revisionists, their previous conviction(s), involvement in large number of criminal cases, no justifiable reason is coming forward for entertaining the plea for suspension of conviction," Justice Gopal held. 
**_Case Title: Mohd Azam Khan v Directorate of Enforcement_**
**_Bench: CJI Kant, Justice Bagchi and Justice Mohana_**
**_Mentioning Date: November 2, 2026_**

# Supreme Court to hear Azam Khan’s plea against ED arrest this week
Azam Khan
By [Muslim Mirror Desk](https://muslimmirror.com/author/bymuslimmirrordesk/)
November 2, 2026
Senior Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan has approached the Supreme Court challenging his arrest by the Enforcement Directorate shortly after his release on bail from Rampur jail in Uttar Pradesh on October 31. The 78-year-old politician’s plea was mentioned urgently before Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Monday, and the court agreed to list it for hearing during the week.
Advocate Nizam Pasha, appearing for Khan, alleged that the arrest was an attempt by the Uttar Pradesh government to keep him in continued custody through “evergreening of cases.” He described the detention as illegal, noting it stemmed from a seven-year-old FIR and formed the 88th case against Khan, who has already been named in 87 FIRs.
Pasha linked the move to the upcoming Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections and claimed it was politically motivated. He reminded the court that the Supreme Court had previously granted Khan relief.
Chief Justice Surya Kant questioned why Khan had directly approached the apex court instead of the Allahabad High Court, which had recently granted him bail. “Have faith in the High Court. It has given him relief. We will relegate this matter to the High Court and request it to take it up without delay,” the CJI observed. Despite this indication, the court directed that the petition be listed during the week.
Khan and his son Abdullah Azam were released on October 29 after the Allahabad High Court suspended their sentences in a dual PAN card case, in which Khan had been sentenced to 10 years. The court, however, refused to stay their convictions. The ED arrested him soon after. A special PMLA court in Ghaziabad then remanded him to 14 days of judicial custody.
The money-laundering case relates to Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur, established by the Jauhar Trust. The ED has alleged diversion of government funds meant for public works towards the university’s construction, claiming Khan used his influence as Urban Development Minister and over the Uttar Pradesh Jal Nigam.
The agency has attached land and buildings linked to the university valued at approximately ₹1,170 crore. The case was registered on the basis of 58 FIRs filed by the state police. Khan has denied the allegations and remains in judicial custody while challenging the arrest.

# SP leader Azam Khan taken into ED custody soon after walking out of Rampur jail
The Allahabad HC had suspended the 10-year prison sentence imposed on Khan and Abdullah in the PAN card fraud case and granted bail to both on October 29.
In this file photo from Sep. 29, 2026, Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Azam Khan speaks to the media in Rampur.(Photo | ANI)
Updated on: 
31 Oct 2026, 3:42 pm
2 min read
  * Copied


LUCKNOW: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Saturday detained senior Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Azam Khan in a money laundering case, shortly after he walked out of Rampur jail on bail in an alleged PAN card fraud case, along with his son, Abdullah Azam, after spending over 11 months in prison.
According to sources, a heated argument ensued between ED officials and Khan for some time before the agency took him into custody and drove him away amid sloganeering by his supporters. His son went home.
Around 15 minutes before Khan's release, an ED team had entered the jail premises amid tight security, with 24 CRPF personnel deployed outside the prison.
The Allahabad High Court had suspended the 10-year prison sentence imposed on Khan and Abdullah in the PAN card case and granted bail to both on October 29.
The ED had registered an FIR against Khan, the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust and others on October 14, following prolonged questioning of the SP leader in jail over alleged unexplained expenditure of Rs 416.14 crore on the construction of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur.
The case was registered at Azeemnagar police station in Rampur district under Sections 61 (criminal conspiracy), 316(5) and 318(4) (criminal breach of trust) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, and Sections 7, 13(1)(d) and 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
The FIR named Khan, the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust, SS and S Enterprises, SS Chik Associates Private Limited and others.
During its probe, the ED had found a significant mismatch between the university's declared expenditure and the assessed value of its construction.
According to ED sources, an Income Tax Department valuation report dated November 10, 2023, estimated the cost of buildings on the campus at Rs 494.46 crore. However, the trust's income-tax returns from FY 2013-14 to FY 2024-25 disclosed capital expenditure of only Rs 78.32 crore, leaving an alleged unexplained gap of Rs 416.14 crore.
Khan's release from jail on Saturday assumes political significance ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections early next year. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav had also met Khan at Rampur jail nine days earlier, on October 22.
Khan was first sent to jail on February 26, 2020. He was released on May 20, 2022, after the Supreme Court granted him interim bail. He was jailed for a second time on October 18, 2023, and released on September 23, 2025. He was sent to jail for a third time on November 17, 2025, and released on October 31, 2026, only to be taken into ED custody again.

# Azam Khan’s brief taste of freedom
BY [Biswajeet Banerjee](https://www.millenniumpost.in/)1 Nov 2026 12:15 AM IST 
[Biswajeet Banerjee](https://www.millenniumpost.in/)1 Nov 2026 12:42 AM IST
**Lucknow/Rampur:** Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan was taken into custody by a team of the Enforcement Directorate (ED) moments after he walked out of Rampur district jail on Saturday evening following his release in the two PAN cards case. His son Abdullah Azam, who was also granted bail in the case, was released from prison.
The ED team, which had reached the jail premises in advance after receiving information about Azam Khan’s impending release, intercepted him as soon as he stepped out of the prison gate around 7 pm. Officials showed him an order before taking him away in their vehicle amid tight security.
Rampur Additional Superintendent of Police Anil Singh Sisodia confirmed that the ED team had taken Azam Khan into custody and was taking him to its headquarters in Ghaziabad for questioning. 
The dramatic development triggered protests by Samajwadi Party workers and Azam Khan’s supporters, who had gathered outside the jail since the afternoon in anticipation of his release. As the ED team surrounded the veteran leader, supporters raised slogans against the agency and expressed their anger over his detention. 
Azam Khan, who was visibly upset, questioned the circumstances surrounding his detention. “What is left to say now? What should I say? The rule of law has ceased to exist. Is this the punishment for being a Muslim? Our mistake was that a Muslim established a university. We built schools for children. Is that our crime?” he said. 
The mood among SP workers, who had been celebrating the expected release of the father-son duo, changed dramatically when the ED team arrived at the jail around 6.15 pm along with a large contingent of paramilitary personnel. 
There was confusion among supporters as Azam Khan was taken away. They later welcomed Abdullah Azam, who walked out of the jail after completing the release formalities. Supporters continued to raise slogans against the ED. 
Azam Khan and Abdullah Azam had been sentenced to seven years in prison each by a district court in the two PAN cards case and were sent to jail on November 17, 2025. The Allahabad High Court granted them bail on October 29 this year. The release process had gained momentum on Friday after the court issued the release warrant. However, uncertainty persisted as warrants in some other cases involving Azam Khan were yet to be issued. His lawyers secured the remaining release orders on Saturday, clearing the way for his release. 
Meanwhile, the ED had registered a fresh case against Azam Khan on October 13 at the Azeem Nagar police station in connection with alleged use of government funds in the construction of Jauhar University and other charges. The fresh case is understood to be linked to the agency’s action against him on Saturday. 
The ED’s move came just as the veteran SP leader was preparing to walk free after nearly 11 months and 14 days in prison.

#  Azam Khan moves Supreme Court against the ED arrest, CJI Surya Kant agrees to hear plea this week 
The jail gate opened on Friday, and so did a new chapter. Azam Khan had barely stepped out with bail in hand when an ED team moved in to detain him. Now the fight has travelled from Rampur to the country’s highest court, where the CJI will decide how soon to listen.
[Statesman News Service](https://www.thestatesman.com/author/authorthestatesman-com) | New Delhi | November 2, 2026 12:51 pm
File Photo 
Samajwadi Party leader Mohd Azam Khan has approached the Supreme Court. He is challenging his arrest by the Enforcement Directorate (ED), which came just as he walked out of jail. The Chief Justice of India has agreed to hear the plea this week.
The matter was mentioned on Monday, November 2, before Chief Justice of India Surya Kant. Advocate Nizam Pasha appeared for Khan. The CJI agreed to list the case for hearing within the week.
Advertisement
Khan is a former Uttar Pradesh minister. His plea questions the way the ED took him into custody. The agency acted moments after he left Rampur jail in a different case.
Advertisement 
## Bail in the dual PAN card case
The sequence began on October 29. The Allahabad High Court granted bail to Khan and his son, Abdullah Azam. The case concerns the alleged possession of two PAN cards.
The court suspended Khan’s 10-year sentence in that case. It did not stay his conviction. So the conviction remains on record even though he was allowed to leave jail.
## Release and detention outside the gate
Khan and his son were released from Rampur jail on October 31. An ED team was already waiting outside. The agency detained Khan as he stepped out.
His son was not taken into custody. The detention was linked to a separate money laundering case, not the dual PAN card matter.
Khan was produced before a special court under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) in Ghaziabad. On Sunday, November 1, the court sent him to 14 days of judicial custody. He therefore remains behind bars despite the bail order from the High Court.
## What the ED case is about
The case centres on Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur. The ED alleges that farmers’ agricultural land was forcibly occupied to build the campus. It says financial irregularities followed.
The agency began its money laundering case on the basis of about 26 first information reports. Uttar Pradesh Police registered these in 2019. Some other reports put the number of FIRs behind the probe at 54.
## The university and the trust
The university was founded in 2006. It is run by the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust, which is headquartered in Lucknow. The trust also runs a public school in Rampur district.
The campus stands at Jauhar Nagar in Singhankhera village. The ED says Khan founded and controls the trust. He is its principal trustee and the honorary chancellor of the university. The institution is named after Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar, a freedom movement figure.
## Raids in August
The ED carried out searches on August 19. About 10 locations were covered. These included sites in Rampur, Saharanpur and Jamia Nagar in Delhi. The trust and the university were among the targets.
Officials seized documents and records from the campus. Khan and Abdullah Azam were already in Rampur jail when the raids took place.
## Property worth Rs 1,170 crore attached
On October 28, the ED announced a provisional attachment. It covered the land and buildings of the university. The agency put the current market value at Rs 1,170 crore.
The ED says public funds, state contracts and government resources were diverted to build the campus. It issued the attachment order under the PMLA. A provisional attachment is not final. It needs confirmation by the adjudicating authority.
That order came just three days before Khan’s release. The arrest followed soon after.
## A long history of scrutiny
This is not the first time the university has drawn action. The ED raided it in July 2019 and seized documents. In September 2023, the Income Tax Department and the ED searched Khan’s home and the campus for three days.
The Rampur Development Authority also raised objections. It said 38 of the 40 buildings on the campus stood without the required approvals.
Khan has faced many cases since 2019. In 2022, he came out of Sitapur jail on interim bail from the Supreme Court. He had spent 27 months in custody by then. Later convictions sent him back to jail.
## What the Supreme Court will examine
The top court will look at whether the arrest after release was lawful. Khan’s side is likely to argue that the ED acted at the exit of the jail to keep him in custody. The agency will point to the PMLA court’s remand order.
The court may also look at how an arrest under the money laundering law can follow bail in another case. PMLA arrests have faced close judicial review in recent years. The outcome could shape how agencies act when a person in jail gets relief in one case.

# Supreme Court Issues Notice On Azam Khan's Plea Challenging Disqualification

Share

**New Delhi:**
The Supreme Court on Monday issued notice on a plea filed by Azam Khan challenging his recent disqualification from the UP Assembly.
A Bench of Justices DY Chandrachud and Hima Kohli said, "Issue notice, returnable on 9 November 2022."
The court said that Garima Prashand, senior counsel appearing for the respondent, shall take instructions, in the meantime.
"Liberty to serve the Standing Counsel for the Election Commission of India, in addition," the court said.
Azam Khan was represented by Senior Advocate P Chidambaram with lawyers Nizam Pasha and Javedur Rahman.
The court was hearing a plea by SP leader Azam Khan challenging his recent disqualification from the UP Assembly.
Azam Khan was earlier disqualified from membership of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly, a day after he was sentenced to 3 years in prison along with a fine of Rs.2,000 in a hate speech case of 2019.

https://courtbook.in/posts/azam-khan-mov.text:
Advertisement
Mohd. Azam Khan has challenged his ED arrest in the Supreme Court after being detained shortly after his release from Rampur jail following an Allahabad High Court bail order.
Advertisement
Samajwadi Party leader Mohd. Azam Khan has approached the Supreme Court challenging his arrest by the Enforcement Directorate (ED), which took him into custody shortly after his release from Rampur jail. The matter was mentioned before Chief Justice of India Surya Kant by advocate Nizam Pasha, and the Chief Justice agreed to take it up for hearing during the week.
## Background
The ED arrested Khan on October 31, 2026, in connection with a money laundering investigation linked to Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur. The investigation concerns alleged financial irregularities associated with the university's construction and development.
Advertisement
The arrest came shortly after Khan and his son, Abdullah Azam Khan, walked out of Rampur jail following an [Allahabad High Court](https://courtbook.in/posts/allahabad-hc-grants-bail-to-azam-khan-and-abdullah-azam-khan-refuses-to-suspend-conviction) order dated October 29. The High Court granted them bail in the dual PAN card cases and suspended their ten-year prison sentences but declined to stay their convictions.
Khan's arrest followed the agency's investigation into alleged financial irregularities involving the university and the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust. The ED's proceedings stem from allegations connected to land acquisition and the use of funds for the institution.
Following his arrest, a special court in Ghaziabad remanded Khan to 14 days of judicial custody on November 1. He was subsequently taken to Dasna District Jail.
During the remand proceedings, Khan's counsel challenged the legality of the ED's action. According to media reports, his lawyer argued that Section 19 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) had been violated in the arrest process. The ED, in response, sought custody for further investigation.
The challenge has now reached the Supreme Court, where advocate Nizam Pasha mentioned the matter before CJI Surya Kant. 
The Chief Justice agreed to list it for hearing this week.

#  In first high-level visit after new government’s arrival, Foreign Secretary Misri to visit Nepal on November 4-5 
## Misri’s visit to include discussions on Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s visit to India; appointment of Nepal’s new Ambassador to India and disaster assistance following the flash floods are also expected to be on the agenda
Published - November 02, 2026 10:48 pm IST - NEW DELHI
[Kallol Bhattacherjee](https://www.thehindu.com/profile/author/kallol-bhattacherjee-680/)
READ LATER
[ SEE ALL ](https://www.thehindu.com/myaccount/?tab=bookmarks) Remove 
Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri on November 2, 2026. (Photo credit: X/@MEAINDIA) 
Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri will pay a two-day visit to Kathmandu on November 4 and 5, the Ministry of External Affairs announced on Monday (November 2, 2026). This will be the first visit by Mr. Misri to Nepal since [Prime Minister Balendra Shah](https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/balendra-shah-enigmatic-mayor/article70468644.ece) took charge in March this year [following the election that was conducted under an interim government.](https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/nepal-election-2026-results-forerunner-balendra-shah-gen-z-protests/article70714599.ece) A visit to India by Mr. Shah is understandably part of the agenda that will be discussed when Mr. Misri meets officials in Kathmandu.
“Foreign Secretary’s upcoming visit continues the tradition of regular high-level exchanges between the two countries and will help further enhance the comprehensive bilateral partnership,” said the Ministry in an announcement. The visit by Mr. Misri to Kathmandu will be keenly watched as it comes amid a slew of reforms that Nepal’s post-Gen-Z uprising government is in the process of rolling out.
[ A new phase in India-Nepal relations](https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/a-new-phase-in-india-nepal-relations/article71080699.ece)
Apart from Mr. Shah’s visit to India, Mr. Misri’s conversations in Kathmandu are likely to feature the appointment of a new Ambassador of Nepal to New Delhi. Nepali Embassy has been without an Ambassador for several months since the previous Ambassador, Shankar Prasad Sharma, returned home. Nepali diplomatic sources told _The Hindu_ earlier that Kathmandu was waiting for the _agrément_ (diplomatic approval) for new envoy Nischal Nath Pandey to take charge in the embassy here. India’s continued assistance to [the disaster in Bhote Koshi river](https://www.thehindu.com/infographics/2026-09-04/nepal-flash-floods-explained/index.html) is also expected to be on the agenda.
Even as Mr. Misri's visit was being announced by the Ministry, a welfare association of former Indian Army soldiers took out a protest in Kathmandu on Monday (November 2) demanding that Gurkha recruitment into the Indian Army be resumed. Recruitment of Gurkha soldiers remains suspended since the Agnipath scheme was introduced by the Government of India.
_The Hindu_ had earlier reported that Mr. Misri was expected to visit Nepal in May, but the visit was postponed ostensibly because Mr. Shah had prioritised domestic challenges. [The India visit by Mr. Shah,](https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/nepal-pm-shah-to-make-meaningful-visit-to-india-date-yet-to-be-finalised-foreign-minister-khanal/article71527885.ece) if it materialises, will be the first bilateral visit abroad by the leader who came into prominence during the September 2025 Gen-Z uprising that overthrew the government of Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli. Mr. Misri had visited Kathmandu previously for two days in August 2025 and had met Mr. Oli.
In the past few months, India has hosted Nepal’s Foreign Minister Sisir Khanal, Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle, and Home Minister Sudan Gurung, who visited Delhi to participate in the first BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) meet held on October 13, 2026. India has also hosted the head of the ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) Rabi Lamichhane in the first week of June when he met Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Mr. Lamichhane paid a personal visit to India last week to pray at the pilgrimage centres in Kainchi Dham in Uttarakhand and the Kamakhya temple in Guwahati.
Mr. Lamichhane had described this visit as “personal and not political”. “There are no political meetings planned. Since this is a personal visit, I urge people not to read politics into it,” said Mr. Lamichhane before starting the visit.

#  Actor Nora Fatehi gets fresh summons in extortion case involving Sukesh Chandrasekhar 
## Additional Sessions Judge Gagandeep Singh issued fresh summons to the actor while expressing displeasure over her non-appearance
Updated  - November 02, 2026 06:06 pm IST - New Delhi
READ LATER
[ SEE ALL ](https://www.thehindu.com/myaccount/?tab=bookmarks) Remove 
Bollywood actor Nora Fatehi attends the ELLE India Beauty Awards on October 27, 2026 | Photo Credit: PTI 
A [Delhi](https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Delhi/) court has summoned actor Nora Fatehi once again as a witness on November 6 in the ₹200-crore extortion case involving alleged conman Sukesh Chandrasekhar.
Additional Sessions Judge Gagandeep Singh issued fresh summons to the actor while expressing displeasure over her non-appearance.
During the proceedings, Nora Fatehi's counsel requested an exemption from her appearance on Monday (November 2, 2026).
[ Aviation firm files ₹3 crore defamation suit against Nora Fatehi for ‘toy plane’ remark](https://www.thehindu.com/entertainment/aviation-firm-files-3-crore-defamation-suit-against-nora-fatehi-for-toy-plane-remark/article71441111.ece)
"This cannot be taken lightly... As a witness, you should have appeared in court; your conduct is not proper, don't take the court for granted...," the judge said.
The Delhi Police informed the court that it had no confirmation about Nora Fatehi's appearance.
They stated that the notice had been served to her on October 22 via email and WhatsApp, and that phone calls had also been made, but there was no response from her.
On October 16, the court said, "Issue summons to Nora Fatehi alias Naura Fatehi (Listed Witness or LW 3 in 3rd Supplementary chargesheet for the said date (of November 2)."
Individual witnesses are initially numbered as LWs and become prosecution witnesses (PWs) after appearing in court.
The case against Mr. Chandrasekhar is being investigated by the Delhi Police Special Cell.
A court had earlier framed charges against Mr. Chandrasekhar, his wife Leena Paulose and others under the Indian Penal Code (IPC) Sections 170 (personating a public servant), 384 (punishment for extortion) and 386 (extortion by putting a person in fear of death or grievous hurt).
Additionally, charges had also been framed under provisions of MCOCA, or the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act, 1999, a law enacted to combat organised crime syndicates and terrorism.
The Act equips authorities with special powers to track, intercept and penalise gang-related criminal activities that normal penal codes fail to deter.
The matter is presently at the stage of the prosecution submitting its evidence.
The police chargesheet had earlier mentioned the recording of statements from several people, including Bollywood actor Jacqueline Fernandez.
Police allege that Mr. Chandrasekhar and his associates reportedly took money from Fortis Healthcare promoter Shivinder Mohan Singh's wife, Aditi Singh, after posing as government officials and promising to secure bail for her husband, who was in jail in a money laundering case.
According to police, Mr. Chandrasekhar allegedly persuaded Aditi to transfer money by impersonating a central government official over a spoofed call. At the same time, he was lodged in Rohini jail and promised to manage bail for her husband.

#  Employees flag procedural gaps in Haryana move to cancel power licence 
Updated  - November 02, 2026 11:21 am IST 
READ LATER
[ SEE ALL ](https://www.thehindu.com/myaccount/?tab=bookmarks) Remove 
Haryana power employees staging a protest against the decision to grant the licence to a private firm. 
More than a week after power employees called off their strike against the grant of a parallel power distribution licence to a private firm in Haryana, a section of the employees’ joint front has raised concerns that a procedural lacuna in the government’s directions seeking cancellation of the licence could allow the company to challenge the move before the appellate tribunal.
The employees fear that the Haryana government’s directions to the Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission (HERC) under Section 108(1) of the Electricity Act, 2003, may not withstand legal scrutiny as they were approved only by Chief Minister Nayab Saini and not by the Council of Ministers.
Indian National Lok Dal patron and former Finance Minister Sampat Singh has also sought clarity on whether the directions under Section 108 were backed by a formal decision of the Council of Ministers under the government’s rules of business.
“The fact that HERC did not provide a hearing to Eleven Power Private Limited before cancelling the parallel licence and the government’s decision has not been approved by the Council of Ministers are enough grounds for the firm to move the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (APTEL). Anticipating this, I have filed a caveat,” he said in a statement.
Following Mr. Saini’s assurance to the striking employees, the Energy Department Secretary, on October 26, directed the HERC “not to create, operationalise or effectuate a parallel distribution licence anywhere in the State of Haryana”. The letter stated that the directions had been issued with the Chief Minister’s approval.
Acting on the directions, the HERC cancelled the 25-year parallel licence granted to Eleven Power for Gurugram and Nuh on October 28. The Commission said it would not proceed further in the matter as long as the government’s directions remained operative.
Eleven Power has since indicated that it would pursue legal remedies. Meanwhile, Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam filed a caveat before the APTEL on October 28, anticipating a legal challenge.
A member of the joint front said its representatives, who participated in the October 23 negotiations with Mr. Saini and Energy Minister Anil Vij, had demanded that the decision be approved by the Council of Ministers. However, they were assured that the Chief Minister’s directions would suffice. Some members now suspect a “conspiracy” to benefit the private firm, the member claimed.
The joint front is likely to meet soon and consider writing to the Chief Minister, seeking Cabinet approval for the decision at its meeting on November 3.
Citing the Karnataka Cabinet’s decision against private participation in power distribution, which led Tata Power to withdraw its application in July this year, the joint front member said Haryana should also secure Cabinet approval for its decision.
Mr. Vij remained unavailable for comment despite repeated attempts to contact him.

#  Police expand search for man who escaped from custody in Coimbatore 
Published - November 01, 2026 08:30 pm IST - COIMBATORE
[ The Hindu Bureau](https://www.thehindu.com/profile/author/the-hindu-bureau-14355/)
READ LATER
[ SEE ALL ](https://www.thehindu.com/myaccount/?tab=bookmarks) Remove 
Searches for Erode native Raghavan (25), who [escaped from the custody of police personnel](https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/tamil-nadu/convict-escapes-from-police-custody-before-being-lodged-in-coimbatore-central-prison/article71648346.ece) escorting him to the Coimbatore Central Prison for judicial remand early on Saturday (October 31, 2026), expanded to more locations on Sunday (November 1, 2026).
Six special teams of the police are on the lookout for Raghavan, who is suspected to have got away in a lorry, shortly after the escape, credible sources said. A surveillance camera visual showed him near an arterial road in Coimbatore, from where he is suspected to have hitched a ride. A senior police officer said that there was no breakthrough in the searches till Sunday evening.
Police sources said Raghavan, who hails from Bhavani in Erode, faces several cases in his native district and in Karnataka. The Erode police had arrested him in one of the cases and he had been lodged in Coimbatore Central Prison in judicial remand. The Karnataka police had taken him to Bengaluru for interrogation in custody. While escorting him back to Coimbatore after the interrogation, Raghavan escaped from them at a place within the jurisdiction of the Annur police (Coimbatore district) on June 19, 2026. The Annur police had registered a case based on the complaint of Karnataka police personnel who escorted him.
According to the Coimbatore District Police, the Annur police traced and arrested Raghavan on Friday (October 30, 2026). The magistrate ordered to remand him in judicial custody. He made a second escape from the police when four personnel were about to take him inside the perimeter wall of the Coimbatore Central Prison at 12.40 a.m. on Saturday.
An officer said a serious security lapse by the escorting personnel resulted in Raghavan’s escape as they were ought to be vigilant, considering the history of the accused.

#  Paliwal takes inspiration from Dogra’s journey 
Updated  - November 02, 2026 09:58 pm IST - New Delhi
[Vivek Krishnan](https://www.thehindu.com/profile/author/vivek-krishnan-24302/)
READ LATER
[ SEE ALL ](https://www.thehindu.com/myaccount/?tab=bookmarks) Remove 
At 34, Rajat Paliwal knows all about the anonymity of domestic cricket. The Services skipper has been the mainstay in his team’s batting unit for over a decade, but the closest he has come to national recognition was when he played for India-A in a four-day clash against West Indies-A in 2013.
Undeterred, Paliwal, who made his Ranji Trophy debut in the 2011-12 season, continues to churn out runs for Services at an average above 40. His latest contribution was an unbeaten 111 against Delhi at the Airforce Complex Ground in Palam on Monday.
When there is little incentive to keep going through the domestic grind, Paliwal takes inspiration from Paras Dogra’s journey. Dogra, 41, had also spent many years in the shadow for teams like Himachal Pradesh and Pondicherry, but finally had his moment in the sun when he led Jammu & Kashmir to a historic Ranji title last season.
“I look at Paras bhai. He has crossed 40. He has been consistently persistent, and won the Ranji title last season. His success after so much hard work makes me also feel good. It does act as a motivation,” Paliwal said on Monday.
Curiously, Paliwal went through his entire innings on day one without the manual scoreboard reflecting his runs. It was an instruction that the Services skipper had passed on to the scoreboard operator.
“I don’t like to take my focus away by knowing my score. I like to keep my concentration on the pitch. I got to know I am nearing a century when Delhi brought the fielders in. It has been my habit post-Covid to not have my score visible,” he said.

# Azam Khan Moves Supreme Court Against ED Arrest Following Release on Bail
By [Law Trend](https://lawtrend.in/author/admin/)
November 2, 2026 11:39 AM
[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Flawtrend.in%2Fazam-khan-moves-supreme-court-against-ed-arrest-following-release-on-bail%2F "Facebook")[WhatsApp](https://api.whatsapp.com/send?text=Azam+Khan+Moves+Supreme+Court+Against+ED+Arrest+Following+Release+on+Bail%20%0A%0A%20https://lawtrend.in/azam-khan-moves-supreme-court-against-ed-arrest-following-release-on-bail/ "WhatsApp")[Twitter](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Azam+Khan+Moves+Supreme+Court+Against+ED+Arrest+Following+Release+on+Bail&url=https%3A%2F%2Flawtrend.in%2Fazam-khan-moves-supreme-court-against-ed-arrest-following-release-on-bail%2F&via=law_trend "Twitter")[Print](https://lawtrend.in/azam-khan-moves-supreme-court-against-ed-arrest-following-release-on-bail/ "Print")[Pinterest](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https://lawtrend.in/azam-khan-moves-supreme-court-against-ed-arrest-following-release-on-bail/&media=https://lawtrend.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/azam-khan-supreme-court.jpeg&description=Azam+Khan+Moves+Supreme+Court+Against+ED+Arrest+Following+Release+on+Bail "Pinterest")
Samajwadi Party leader Mohd Azam Khan has challenged his arrest by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) before the Supreme Court, after the agency detained him outside Rampur jail shortly following his release on bail in a separate criminal case.
The matter was mentioned before Chief Justice of India Surya Kant by advocate Nizam Pasha. The Chief Justice agreed to take up the case for hearing this week.
Khan was arrested on October 31 in connection with a money laundering investigation involving alleged financial irregularities linked to Mohammad Ali Jauhar University.

A special Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) court in Ghaziabad subsequently remanded him to 14 days of judicial custody on November 1.
**Arrest Followed High Court Bail Order**
The ED detained Khan shortly after he and his son Abdullah Azam were released from Rampur jail on October 31.
Their release followed an October 29 order of the Allahabad High Court granting them bail in the dual PAN card case.
While granting relief, the High Court suspended Khan’s 10-year prison sentence in the case but declined to stay his conviction.
An ED team waiting outside Rampur jail took Khan into custody in connection with the separate money laundering proceedings.

**Money Laundering Case Linked to Jauhar University**
The ED investigation concerns allegations that agricultural land belonging to farmers was forcibly occupied for Mohammad Ali Jauhar University.
The agency initiated money laundering proceedings against Khan and others on the basis of approximately 26 first information reports (FIRs) registered by the Uttar Pradesh Police in 2019.
Khan has now approached the Supreme Court questioning his arrest immediately after securing release from prison in the dual PAN card case. His challenge is expected to be heard this week.

# Supreme Court gave justice: SP leader Azam Khan's son Abdullah Azam Khan on bail order
  * [TN National Desk](https://www.timesnownews.com/author/TN%20National%20Desk-479257182)
  * Updated: May 20, 2022, 07:37 IST


## SP leader Azam Khan was booked along with others for allegedly grabbing enemy property and misappropriating public money of hundreds of crores of rupees. He was in Sitapur jail in connection with several other cases as well.
SP leader Azam Khan's son Abdullah Azam Khan welomed the Supreme Court's decision of granting bail
Photo : ANI
[follow us](https://profile.google.com/cp/CgkvbS8wZ3NmeHE)[follow us](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029Va7R81560eBdf7e61g0T)
**Sitapur :** After the Supreme Court on Thursday granted interim bail to Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Azam Khan, police tightened the vigil outside Sitapur district jail ahead of his release on Friday. The SP leader was granted bail in a case concerning the Kotwali police station in Rampur, Uttar Pradesh. Azam Khan's son, Adeeb Azam Khan welcomed the Supreme Court's decision and noted that they will directly go to Rampur after the release.
## 'Supreme Court delivered justice'
"I am very happy (with Supreme Court's order). Will go to Rampur directly (after the release)," said Adeeb Azam Khan. Notably, the jailed SP leader's sons, Adeeb Azam Khan and Abdullah Azam Khan reached the Sitapur district jail ahead of his release today. Abdullah Azam Khan noted that the 'Supreme Court delivered justice.'
## 'Habitual offender'
The Supreme Court granted bail to Azam Khan two days after the UP government urged the court to deny the same. Opposing his bail on Tuesday, the Yogi Aditynath's government called Azam Khan a "land grabber" and a "habitual offender."
"He is a land grabber. Private complaints have been filed against him. He is a habitual offender. Everything is forged by this person," Additional Solicitor General SV Raju, representing the Uttar Pradesh government told the SC bench headed by Justice L Nageswara Rao.
The Supreme Court on Thursday gave the SP leader a period of two weeks to apply for regular bail before the concerned court.
Notably, SP leader Azam Khan was booked along with others for allegedly grabbing enemy property and misappropriating public money of hundreds of crores of rupees. He was in Sitapur jail in connection with several other cases as well.

# Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan released from Sitapur jail
  * [TN National Desk](https://www.timesnownews.com/author/TN%20National%20Desk-479257182)
  * Updated: May 20, 2022, 08:57 IST


## On Thursday, a bench of justices L Nageswara Rao, BR Gavai, AS Bopanna granted interim bail to Azam Khan, and also granted him the liberty to apply for regular bail before the concerned court within a period of two weeks. The Supreme Court also assured that the interim bail will be continued until the regular bail is decided by the competent court.
Azam Khan is presently lodged in Sitapur jail in connection with several cases, including land grabbing, against him in Rampur. (File image)
Photo : PTI
[follow us](https://profile.google.com/cp/CgkvbS8wZ3NmeHE)[follow us](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029Va7R81560eBdf7e61g0T)
Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan was released from Sitapur district jail on Friday, a day after the Supreme Court granted him interim bail in an alleged case of cheating, relating to Kotwali police station in Uttar Pradesh.
He was received by Pragatisheel Samajwadi Party (Lohiya) leader Shivpal Singh Yadav, his son and MLA Abdullah Azam and a large number of supporters. After the release, Khan left for his native Rampur.
Shivpal Singh Yadav had left for Sitapur early on Friday morning to receive Khan on his release. "A new sun is rising on the state's horizon," he tweeted.
On Thursday, a bench of justices L Nageswara Rao, BR Gavai, AS Bopanna granted interim bail to Khan, and also granted him the liberty to apply for regular bail before the concerned court within a period of two weeks.
> #WATCH | Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan released from Sitapur district jail, in a matter concerning Kotwali PS in… [t.co/HkRmbAHACm](https://t.co/HkRmbAHACm)
> — ANI (@ANI) [May 20, 2022](https://twitter.com/ANI/status/1527478498062831616?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)
The Supreme Court also assured that the interim bail will be continued until the regular bail is decided by the competent court.
“The interim bail granted to the petitioner by the present order shall continue to operate till the decision of the competent court in the application for regular bail and in the event that the regular bail application is decided against the interest of the petitioner, the present interim bail shall continue to operate for a further period of two weeks from the date of the order passed by the Competent Court in the application for regular bail,” the bench said.
Khan is presently lodged in Sitapur jail in connection with several cases, including land grabbing, against him in Rampur.
The apex courthad earlier expressed displeasure over the delay in the announcement of judgement by Allahabad high court on Khan’s bail plea and called it a ‘travesty of justice’.
Last week, the Allahabad HC had granted Khan interim bail in the case related to wrongful possession of land.
Ahead of the release of Khan on Friday, police tightened vigil outside Sitapur district jail.

> — ANI (@ANI) [May 20, 2022](https://twitter.com/ANI/status/1527439068354646016?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)
Adeeb Azam Khan, son of the SP leader, said, "I am very happy (with Supreme Court's order)."
" Will go to Rampur directly (after the release)," Adeeb told reporters outside the jail.

# Azam Khan Release: After SC granted interim bail, SP leader walks out of Sitapur jail
| Updated on: 20 May 2022, 9:48 IST 
SP leader Azam Khan (File Pic)

[Samajwadi Party](https://www.catchnews.com/topic/samajwadi-party/) leader Azam Khan was released from Sitapur district jail on Friday, a day after the Supreme Court granted him interim bail in an alleged case of cheating.
The SP leader was granted bail in a cheating case lodged at the police station in Rampur.
The Supreme Court also ordered that Azam Khan be released until the regular bail is decided by the competent court.
"The Supreme Court gave justice," said Azam Khan's son Abdullah Azam Khan.
Azam Khan's son, Adeeb Azam Khan, welcomed the Supreme Court's decision and noted that they will directly go to Rampur after the release.
"I am very happy (with Supreme Court's order). We will go to Rampur directly (after the release)," said Adeeb Azam Khan, son of SP leader Azam Khan.
Earlier on Thursday, the Supreme Court granted interim bail to Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan in another case of cheating.
A bench of justices L Nageswara Rao, BR Gavai, AS Bopanna granted interim bail to Khan and also allowed him to apply for regular bail before the concerned court within two weeks.
Earlier on Tuesday, the apex court had reserved the order on Khan's interim bail plea in the aforesaid case, as opposed by the Additional Solicitor General SV Raju, appearing for Uttar Pradesh state.
The Supreme Court had earlier expressed displeasure with the prolonged delay in the announcement of judgment by Allahabad HC on his (Khan's) bail plea and called it a 'travesty of justice'.
Last week, the Allahabad HC had granted Khan interim bail in the case related to wrongful possession of land.
Khan was lodged in Sitapur jail since February 2020 as many cases are registered against him.
(ANI)
